- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- codemyspec:design: Architecture design, UI design system, and technology strategy. Use before writing code to plan how to build it.
- codemyspec:develop: Full-lifecycle development — context orchestration, LiveView orchestration, and interactive refactoring. Spawns subagents for multi-step workflows.
- codemyspec:implement: Autonomous implementation loop — start or stop requirements-driven development. The agent walks the requirement graph automatically.
- codemyspec:init: Project setup, authentication, and sync. Use when starting a new project, logging in, or refreshing stale state.
- codemyspec:next: Find and start the next requirement task in one gesture. Use after each completed task as your single onboarding instruction.
- codemyspec:product: Product management — guided story interview, review, and Three Amigos sessions. Use when defining what to build, refining requirements, reviewing story quality, or running an Example Mapping session on a story.
- codemyspec:qa: QA testing and issue management — full app QA, per-story QA, integration planning, issue triage, and fixes.
- codemyspec:sync: Sync project components and regenerate architecture views. Use after git pulls, before design sessions, or when views feel stale.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures do
  @moduledoc """
  Curated bridge from BDD specs into in-app state.

  The only module that may dep on `CleanerCrm` from inside the spex test
  tree. Declared as its own top-level Boundary so the spec boundary
  (`CleanerCrmSpex`) can dep on it without inheriting `CleanerCrm`'s deps.

  Keep this list small — every export is a sanctioned shortcut past the
  UI, used only for `given_` state that has its own covered creation flow.
  """

  use Boundary, top_level?: true, deps: [CleanerCrm, CleanerCrmTest]

  # These contexts are specified in the architecture but not yet
  # implemented — the red BDD specs that call these fixtures exist to
  # drive their implementation. Remove entries as each context lands.
  @compile {:no_warn_undefined,
            [
              CleanerCrm.Clients,
              CleanerCrm.Scheduling,
              CleanerCrm.Billing,
              CleanerCrm.TimeTracking,
              CleanerCrm.Notifications
            ]}

  # Auth/session seeding — registration and login have their own specs;
  # every other spec starts from an existing confirmed user.
  defdelegate user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate valid_user_password(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate set_password(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  # Tenant seeding — account creation has its own spec; other specs need
  # an existing company (account) to scope against.
  # Uncertain export: prune if account specs end up seeding via the UI.
  def account_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, account} =
      CleanerCrm.Accounts.create_account(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})
      )

    account
  end

  # Session — logs a fixture user into a conn. Login itself has its
  # own auth specs; every other spec starts from an authenticated conn.
  defdelegate log_in_user(conn, user), to: CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase

  # Scheduling (story 834) — a cleaner is an account member who gets
  # assigned jobs. No creation flow covers this yet: `ScheduleLive.Board`
  # (the board's own assign/reassign UI) doesn't exist. Sanctioned
  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — prune once the board can seed
  # cleaner assignment directly.
  def cleaner_fixture(scope, account, attrs \\ %{}) do
    user = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture(attrs)
    {:ok, _member} = CleanerCrm.Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account.id, :member)
    user
  end

  # Billing (story 836) — client, job, and invoice seeding.
  #
  # Job completion generating its invoice is covered end-to-end by
  # story 836's own "completing a job generates its invoice" spec
  # (drives FieldLive.Job -> InvoiceLive). Scenarios whose subject is
  # a downstream invoice-collection decision (charging a card,
  # payment links, declines, webhook confirmation) seed the completed
  # job and its invoice directly here instead of re-driving job
  # completion every time — a sanctioned shortcut per
  # bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def client_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, client} =
      CleanerCrm.Clients.create_client(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          name: "Client #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}",
          card_on_file: false
        })
      )

    client
  end

  def job_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, job} =
      CleanerCrm.Scheduling.create_job(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          agreed_price: Decimal.new("150.00"),
          status: :scheduled
        })
      )

    job
  end

  # `given_` blocks bind `scope` from `user_scope_fixture/1` *before*
  # `account_fixture/2` creates the account, so it never carries an
  # `active_account_id` — every fixture below that scopes a context
  # call by account needs to resolve it from the user's membership at
  # call time instead of trusting the scope it was handed.
  defp scoped_to_account(%CleanerCrm.Users.Scope{active_account_id: nil, user: user} = scope) do
    case CleanerCrm.Accounts.MembersRepository.list_user_accounts(user.id) do
      [account | _] -> %{scope | active_account_id: account.id, active_account: account}
      [] -> scope
    end
  end

  defp scoped_to_account(scope), do: scope

  def job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    job = job_fixture(scope, client, Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :completed}))

    {:ok, _checklist} =
      CleanerCrm.Quality.complete_checklist(scope, job, [
        %{
          task: "Kitchen counters wiped down",
          before_photo: "before_kitchen.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_kitchen.jpg"
        },
        %{
          task: "Bathrooms sanitized",
          before_photo: "before_bath.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_bath.jpg"
        }
      ])

    job
  end

  def invoice_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, invoice} =
      CleanerCrm.Billing.create_invoice(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          amount: job.agreed_price,
          status: :unpaid
        })
      )

    invoice
  end

  # Time tracking (story 838) — a resolved clock-in/out record for a
  # job.
  #
  # Clocking in and out through the UI is covered end-to-end by story
  # 838's own "cleaner clocks in and out of an assigned job" spec
  # (drives FieldLive.Job). Scenarios whose subject is a downstream pay
  # calculation (hourly vs. piece-rate, running pay-period totals,
  # payroll CSV export) seed the resolved time entry directly here
  # instead of re-driving the clock-in/out flow every time — a
  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def time_entry_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, time_entry} =
      CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.create_time_entry(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-08 09:00:00Z],
          clocked_out_at: ~U[2024-01-08 12:00:00Z]
        })
      )

    time_entry
  end

  # Notifications (story 837) — an already-sent appointment reminder
  # with its confirm/reschedule token.
  #
  # The automatic "reminder sent at the configured lead time" trigger
  # is covered end-to-end by story 837's own "reminder fires at the
  # configured lead time" spec. Scenarios whose subject is a
  # downstream decision on an existing reminder (confirm, reschedule,
  # delivery-status fallback) seed the already-sent notification
  # directly here instead of re-driving the scheduler trigger every
  # time — a sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def notification_fixture(scope, client, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, notification} =
      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          job_id: job.id,
          kind: :reminder,
          channel: :email,
          status: :sent,
          token: "reminder_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
        })
      )

    notification
  end

  # Schedule alerts (story 843) — a pending schedule-change
  # notification already pushed to a cleaner.
  #
  # The push itself (a moved or cancelled job creating this
  # notification) is covered end-to-end by story 843's own "moved job
  # notifies the cleaner" / "cancelled job notifies the cleaner"
  # specs, which drive the real trigger via `ScheduleLive.Board`.
  # Scenarios whose subject is a downstream decision on an existing
  # pending change (acknowledging, re-prompting, office visibility,
  # escalation, channel fallback) seed the already-pushed notification
  # directly here instead of re-driving the board move every time — a
  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md. Never pass
  # `status: :acknowledged` here — the acknowledgment round-trip
  # through `FieldLive.Today` is the whole point of story 843.
  def schedule_change_notification_fixture(scope, cleaner, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, notification} =
      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
          job_id: job.id,
          kind: :schedule_change,
          channel: :push,
          status: :pending,
          change_summary: "Job schedule changed",
          pushed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
          token: "schedule_change_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
        })
      )

    notification
  end

  # Quality (story 839) — a job carrying an unfinished, per-job
  # checklist of required and optional tasks.
  #
  # Checking items off and completing the job through the checklist UI
  # is the subject under test in `FieldLive.Job`, so this fixture stops
  # short of that — it only seeds the checklist itself. Sanctioned
  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md: `ChecklistTemplate` assignment
  # (story 842) has its own creation flow this fixture skips.
  def job_with_checklist_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, attrs \\ %{}) do
    job =
      job_fixture(
        scope,
        client,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :in_progress, cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
      )

    {:ok, checklist} =
      CleanerCrm.Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, [
        %{task: "Kitchen counters wiped down", required: true},
        %{task: "Bathrooms sanitized", required: true},
        %{task: "Fridge interior wiped down", required: false}
      ])

    %{job: job, checklist: checklist}
  end

  # Quality (story 842) — a job carrying an unfinished, room-grouped
  # checklist whose items are exactly what the caller passes in.
  #
  # Story 842 owns the `ChecklistTemplate` -> per-job `Checklist`
  # assignment flow (which room/task combinations count as in scope for
  # a given job). That assignment UI doesn't exist yet and isn't part
  # of this story's component list (only `FieldLive.ChecklistComponent`
  # is), so seeding the already-instantiated, room-tagged checklist
  # directly is the sanctioned bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — the
  # subject under test is opening/working the checklist on
  # `FieldLive.Job`, not how it got assigned. `items` is a list of
  # `%{room:, task:, required:}` maps; a spec proving an out-of-scope
  # task never appears simply omits it from `items`.
  def job_with_room_checklist_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, items, attrs \\ %{}) do
    job =
      job_fixture(
        scope,
        client,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :in_progress, cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
      )

    {:ok, checklist} = CleanerCrm.Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, items)

    %{job: job, checklist: checklist}
  end
end

=== test/spex/840_see_an_audit_trail_of_schedule_and_record_changes/criterion_7193_office_staff_reschedules_a_job_and_it_is_logged_spex.exs ===
defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story840.Criterion7193Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 840 — See an audit trail of schedule and record changes
  Criterion 7193 — Office staff reschedules a job and it is logged: an
  audit entry records who moved the job, the old and new times, and
  the timestamp of the change.

  Assumes `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.JobFormComponent` (per the
  project's architecture spec, opened from the board at `/schedule`)
  exposes a `[data-test='job-<id>-edit-button']` trigger and a
  `[data-test='job-form']` submitted via `render_submit` with
  `scheduled_date`/`start_time`/`end_time` fields. Assumes
  `CleanerCrmWeb.AuditLive` (`/audit`) renders a
  `[data-test='audit-entries']` list where each entry shows its actor,
  action, one `"<Field label>: <old> → <new>"` line per changed field,
  and today's date as its timestamp.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "office staff reschedules a job and it is logged" do
    scenario "moving a job from Tuesday 9:00 to Wednesday 1:00 pm is recorded" do
      given_ "office staffer Dana is logged in with an active account", context do
        user =
          Fixtures.user_fixture(%{
            email: "dana-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a job is scheduled for Tuesday at 9:00 am", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{name: "Tuesday client"})

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            scheduled_date: tuesday(),
            start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
            end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, job: job})}
      end

      when_ "Dana moves the job to Wednesday at 1:00 pm", context do
        {:ok, board_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        board_live
        |> element("[data-test='job-#{context.job.id}-edit-button']")
        |> render_click()

        board_live
        |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
          job: %{
            scheduled_date: Date.to_iso8601(wednesday()),
            start_time: "13:00",
            end_time: "15:00"
          }
        )
        |> render_submit()

        {:ok, context}
      end

      when_ "the owner filters the audit trail to that job over the past week", context do
        {:ok, audit_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/audit")

        audit_live
        |> form("[data-test='audit-filter-form']",
          filter: %{
            subject_id: to_string(context.job.id),
            date_from: Date.to_iso8601(Date.add(Date.utc_today(), -7)),
            date_to: Date.to_iso8601(Date.utc_today())
          }
        )
        |> render_change()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :audit_live, audit_live)}
      end

      then_ "the owner sees which user deleted the job and when", context do
        html = render(context.audit_live)

        assert html =~ context.user.email
        assert html =~ "deleted"
        assert html =~ "Friday client"
        assert html =~ Date.to_iso8601(Date.utc_today())

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end

  defp friday do
    today = Date.utc_today()
    monday = Date.add(today, -(Date.day_of_week(today) - 1))
    Date.add(monday, 4)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling do
  @moduledoc """
  Recurring plans and the jobs they generate, cleaner time-off, and
  conflict-aware assignment.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{
    AvailabilityBlock,
    ConflictDetector,
    Job,
    Recurrence,
    RecurringPlan
  }

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  ## Jobs

  def get_job!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_job(%Scope{}, %Job{} = job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Job.changeset(job, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a job. Recorded in the audit trail as authored by the
  caller, unless `actor: :system` is passed — used when the job is one
  occurrence materialized from a recurring plan rather than a job a
  human directly asked for (see `create_recurring_plan/2`).
  """
  def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs, opts \\ [])
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, job} <-
           %Job{account_id: account_id}
           |> Job.changeset(attrs)
           |> Repo.insert() do
      record_job_created(scope, job, Keyword.get(opts, :actor, :user))
      {:ok, job}
    end
  end

  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :system) do
    Recorder.record_system(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
  end

  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :user) do
    Recorder.record(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
  end

  defp job_created_values(job) do
    %{"scheduled_date" => to_string(job.scheduled_date), "cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id}
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every job scheduled between `week_start` and six days later,
  cleaner/property/client preloaded, ordered for the board.
  """
  def list_jobs_for_week(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Date{} = week_start)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    week_end = Date.add(week_start, 6)

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date >= ^week_start and
        j.scheduled_date <= ^week_end and j.status != :cancelled
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every non-cancelled job for the account, cleaner/property/client
  preloaded, ordered for the board. Unlike `list_jobs_for_week/2`, this
  isn't bounded to a single week — a recurring plan's series can span
  months, and the board needs to account for all of it at a glance.
  """
  def list_jobs(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id and j.status != :cancelled)
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Assigns (or reassigns) a job to a cleaner, rejecting the move with
  `{:error, :unavailable}` or `{:error, :overlap}` when it conflicts
  with that cleaner's time off or an existing booking. A `nil`
  `cleaner_id` always succeeds (unassigning never conflicts).
  """
  def assign_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <-
           ConflictDetector.check_assignment(
             scope,
             cleaner_id,
             job.scheduled_date,
             job.start_time,
             job.end_time,
             exclude_job_id: job.id
           ),
         {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_reassigned",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id},
        %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def cancel_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_cancelled",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  ## Recurring plans

  def get_recurring_plan!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    RecurringPlan
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:property, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_recurring_plan(%Scope{}, %RecurringPlan{} = plan, attrs \\ %{}) do
    RecurringPlan.preview_changeset(plan, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Runs conflict detection for a (possibly unsaved) plan's full series
  against its preferred cleaner, without persisting anything. Returns
  only the conflicting occurrences, as `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
  """
  def preview_conflicts(scope, %RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
    ConflictDetector.check_occurrences(scope, plan, Recurrence.occurrences(plan))
  end

  @doc """
  Saves a recurring plan and materializes its full series of jobs.
  Conflicting occurrences are still created and still assigned to the
  preferred cleaner — conflicts are for the owner to review and
  resolve, never a silent block on saving.
  """
  def create_recurring_plan(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, plan} <-
             %RecurringPlan{account_id: account_id}
             |> RecurringPlan.changeset(attrs)
             |> Repo.insert() do
        jobs =
          plan
          |> Recurrence.job_attrs()
          |> Enum.map(fn job_attrs ->
            {:ok, job} = create_job(scope, job_attrs, actor: :system)
            job
          end)

        {:ok, {plan, jobs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  ## Availability blocks

  def change_availability_block(%Scope{}, %AvailabilityBlock{} = block, attrs \\ %{}) do
    AvailabilityBlock.changeset(block, attrs)
  end

  def create_availability_block(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %AvailabilityBlock{account_id: account_id}
    |> AvailabilityBlock.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Cleaners (account members who take jobs)

  @doc """
  Lists the account's members as candidate cleaners for the board and
  assignment pickers.
  """
  def list_cleaners(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> Accounts.list_account_members(account_id)
    |> Enum.map(& &1.user)
  end

  @doc """
  Registers a new cleaner: a user identified by display name (rather
  than login credentials) added to the account as a member, so jobs
  and availability can be assigned to them. There is no login flow for
  a cleaner created this way — see `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3`
  for the (real, login-capable) path other stories seed cleaners
  through.
  """
  def register_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, name)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(name) do
    with {:ok, user} <- insert_cleaner_user(name),
         {:ok, _member} <- Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account_id, :member) do
      {:ok, user}
    end
  end

  defp insert_cleaner_user(name) do
    %User{}
    |> Ecto.Changeset.cast(%{name: name, email: placeholder_email(name)}, [:name, :email])
    |> Ecto.Changeset.validate_required([:name, :email])
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp placeholder_email(name) do
    slug =
      name
      |> String.downcase()
      |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]+/, ".")
      |> String.trim(".")

    "#{slug}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@cleaners.local"
  end
end

1	defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  A single scheduled visit: a property (or client), a time window, and
4	  an optional assigned cleaner.
5	
6	  A job is either a one-off (`recurring_plan_id` is `nil`) or one
7	  occurrence materialized from a `RecurringPlan`'s cadence (see
8	  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence`). Both `client_id` and
9	  `property_id` are independently optional at the schema level — some
10	  callers (time tracking, quality, notifications) only ever have a
11	  client on hand, while the schedule board's own job form always
12	  carries a property.
13	
14	  ## Status
15	
16	  `:scheduled` (default) -> `:in_progress` -> `:completed`, or
17	  `:scheduled` -> `:cancelled`. Transitions beyond create/cancel belong
18	  to other contexts (time tracking clocks a job into `:in_progress`).
19	
20	  ## Pay fields
21	
22	  `pay_type`/`hourly_rate_cents`/`piece_rate_cents` describe what the
23	  *cleaner* earns for this job — as distinct from `agreed_price_cents`,
24	  what the *client* is charged. They live here rather than on a
25	  separate table for the same reason `agreed_price_cents` does: a
26	  job's pay arrangement is a one-off property of that job, read and
27	  written by `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking` rather than by Scheduling
28	  itself.
29	  """
30	
31	  use Ecto.Schema
32	  import Ecto.Changeset
33	
34	  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
35	          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
36	          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
37	          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
38	          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
39	          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
40	          recurring_plan_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
41	          scheduled_date: Date.t() | nil,
42	          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
43	          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
44	          status: :scheduled | :in_progress | :completed | :cancelled,
45	          agreed_price_cents: integer() | nil,
46	          pay_type: :hourly | :piece_rate | nil,
47	          hourly_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
48	          piece_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
49	          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
50	          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
51	        }
52	
53	  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
54	  schema "jobs" do
55	    field :scheduled_date, :date
56	    field :start_time, :time
57	    field :end_time, :time
58	
59	    field :status, Ecto.Enum,
60	      values: [:scheduled, :in_progress, :completed, :cancelled],
61	      default: :scheduled
62	
63	    field :agreed_price_cents, :integer
64	    field :agreed_price, :decimal, virtual: true
65	
66	    field :pay_type, Ecto.Enum, values: [:hourly, :piece_rate]
67	    field :hourly_rate_cents, :integer
68	    field :piece_rate_cents, :integer
69	
70	    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
71	    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id
72	    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
73	    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User
74	    belongs_to :recurring_plan, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan, type: :binary_id
75	
76	    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
77	  end
78	
79	  @fields ~w(client_id property_id cleaner_id recurring_plan_id scheduled_date
80	             start_time end_time status agreed_price_cents agreed_price
81	             pay_type hourly_rate_cents piece_rate_cents)a
82	
83	  def changeset(job, attrs) do
84	    job
85	    |> cast(rename_date_key(attrs), @fields)
86	    |> validate_required([:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])
87	    |> validate_time_order()
88	    |> put_agreed_price_cents()
89	  end
90

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job do
  @moduledoc """
  A single scheduled visit: a property (or client), a time window, and
  an optional assigned cleaner.

  A job is either a one-off (`recurring_plan_id` is `nil`) or one
  occurrence materialized from a `RecurringPlan`'s cadence (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence`). Both `client_id` and
  `property_id` are independently optional at the schema level — some
  callers (time tracking, quality, notifications) only ever have a
  client on hand, while the schedule board's own job form always
  carries a property.

  ## Status

  `:scheduled` (default) -> `:in_progress` -> `:completed`, or
  `:scheduled` -> `:cancelled`. Transitions beyond create/cancel belong
  to other contexts (time tracking clocks a job into `:in_progress`).

  ## Pay fields

  `pay_type`/`hourly_rate_cents`/`piece_rate_cents` describe what the
  *cleaner* earns for this job — as distinct from `agreed_price_cents`,
  what the *client* is charged. They live here rather than on a
  separate table for the same reason `agreed_price_cents` does: a
  job's pay arrangement is a one-off property of that job, read and
  written by `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking` rather than by Scheduling
  itself.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          recurring_plan_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          scheduled_date: Date.t() | nil,
          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          status: :scheduled | :in_progress | :completed | :cancelled,
          agreed_price_cents: integer() | nil,
          pay_type: :hourly | :piece_rate | nil,
          hourly_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          piece_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "jobs" do
    field :scheduled_date, :date
    field :start_time, :time
    field :end_time, :time

    field :status, Ecto.Enum,
      values: [:scheduled, :in_progress, :completed, :cancelled],
      default: :scheduled

    field :agreed_price_cents, :integer
    field :agreed_price, :decimal, virtual: true

    field :pay_type, Ecto.Enum, values: [:hourly, :piece_rate]
    field :hourly_rate_cents, :integer
    field :piece_rate_cents, :integer

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User
    belongs_to :recurring_plan, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(client_id property_id cleaner_id recurring_plan_id scheduled_date
             start_time end_time status agreed_price_cents agreed_price
             pay_type hourly_rate_cents piece_rate_cents)a

  def changeset(job, attrs) do
    job
    |> cast(rename_date_key(attrs), @fields)
    |> validate_required([:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])
    |> validate_time_order()
    |> put_agreed_price_cents()
  end

  # The board's own job form asks for a plain "date" — friendlier than
  # "scheduled date" — while every other caller (fixtures, other
  # contexts) uses the schema's real field name directly.
  defp rename_date_key(%{"date" => date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete("date") |> Map.put("scheduled_date", date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{date: date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete(:date) |> Map.put(:scheduled_date, date)

  defp rename_date_key(attrs), do: attrs

  defp validate_time_order(changeset) do
    start_time = get_field(changeset, :start_time)
    end_time = get_field(changeset, :end_time)

    if start_time && end_time && Time.compare(start_time, end_time) != :lt do
      add_error(changeset, :end_time, "must be after the start time")
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  # `agreed_price` arrives as dollars (a `Decimal`, matching the
  # money-handling ADR's rate math); it is rounded half-up and stored
  # as `agreed_price_cents` — the only column ever persisted.
  defp put_agreed_price_cents(changeset) do
    case get_change(changeset, :agreed_price) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      %Decimal{} = amount ->
        cents = amount |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer()
        put_change(changeset, :agreed_price_cents, cents)
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder do
  @moduledoc """
  API other contexts call to append audit trail entries.

  Callers pass the acting scope, an action string, the subject being
  changed, and old/new value maps. Nothing here ever updates or deletes
  a row — this module only ever inserts.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.AuditEntry
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  @doc """
  Records an audit entry attributed to the scope's current user.
  """
  def record(
        %Scope{} = scope,
        action,
        subject_type,
        subject_id,
        old_value \\ %{},
        new_value \\ %{}
      )
      when is_binary(action) and is_binary(subject_type) do
    insert(scope, %{system: false, actor_id: scope.user && scope.user.id}, action, subject_type,
      subject_id: subject_id,
      old_value: old_value,
      new_value: new_value
    )
  end

  @doc """
  Records an audit entry attributed to the system rather than a human
  actor — for automated processes such as recurring job materialization.
  """
  def record_system(
        %Scope{} = scope,
        action,
        subject_type,
        subject_id,
        old_value \\ %{},
        new_value \\ %{}
      )
      when is_binary(action) and is_binary(subject_type) do
    insert(scope, %{system: true, actor_id: nil}, action, subject_type,
      subject_id: subject_id,
      old_value: old_value,
      new_value: new_value
    )
  end

  defp insert(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, actor_attrs, action, subject_type, rest)
       when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %AuditEntry{}
    |> AuditEntry.changeset(
      Map.merge(actor_attrs, %{
        account_id: account_id,
        action: action,
        subject_type: subject_type,
        subject_id: rest[:subject_id],
        old_value: rest[:old_value],
        new_value: rest[:new_value]
      })
    )
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists audit entries for a subject, most recent first.
  """
  def list_for_subject(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, subject_type, subject_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(subject_type) do
    AuditEntry
    |> where(
      [e],
      e.account_id == ^account_id and e.subject_type == ^subject_type and
        e.subject_id == ^subject_id
    )
    |> order_by([e], desc: e.inserted_at)
    |> preload(:actor)
    |> Repo.all()
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Audit do
  @moduledoc """
  Read-side of the append-only audit trail: filtered listing of the
  entries `CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder` appends.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.AuditEntry
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  @doc """
  Lists the account's audit entries, most recent first, optionally
  narrowed by a filter map (string or atom keys):

  - `:subject_id` — exact match against the subject the entry is about
  - `:date_from` — inclusive lower bound (a `Date` or an ISO 8601 string)
  - `:date_to` — inclusive upper bound (a `Date` or an ISO 8601 string)

  A blank or absent value for any key leaves that filter off.
  """
  def list_entries(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, filters \\ %{})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    AuditEntry
    |> where([e], e.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> filter_by_subject(fetch(filters, :subject_id))
    |> filter_by_date_from(fetch(filters, :date_from))
    |> filter_by_date_to(fetch(filters, :date_to))
    |> order_by([e], desc: e.inserted_at)
    |> preload(:actor)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  defp fetch(filters, key), do: Map.get(filters, key) || Map.get(filters, to_string(key))

  defp filter_by_subject(query, blank) when blank in [nil, ""], do: query

  defp filter_by_subject(query, subject_id),
    do: where(query, [e], e.subject_id == ^subject_id)

  defp filter_by_date_from(query, blank) when blank in [nil, ""], do: query

  defp filter_by_date_from(query, %Date{} = date),
    do: where(query, [e], e.inserted_at >= ^start_of_day(date))

  defp filter_by_date_from(query, date_string) when is_binary(date_string),
    do: filter_by_date_from(query, Date.from_iso8601!(date_string))

  defp filter_by_date_to(query, blank) when blank in [nil, ""], do: query

  defp filter_by_date_to(query, %Date{} = date),
    do: where(query, [e], e.inserted_at < ^start_of_day(Date.add(date, 1)))

  defp filter_by_date_to(query, date_string) when is_binary(date_string),
    do: filter_by_date_to(query, Date.from_iso8601!(date_string))

  defp start_of_day(date), do: DateTime.new!(date, ~T[00:00:00], "Etc/UTC")
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story832.Criterion7111Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 832 — Manage clients and properties with access details
  Criterion 7111 — A job scheduled at a property inherits that
  property's access details (entry codes, parking notes, pet notes)
  into its brief.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "job brief inherits property access details" do
    scenario "scheduling a job at a property carries its access details into the brief" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a property with lockbox code \"4821\", parking note \"driveway only\", and pet note \"dog in yard\"",
             context do
        client_path = create_client(context.conn, "Devon Ashe")

        property_path =
          create_property(context.conn, client_path, %{
            service_address: "77 Maple Ave",
            lockbox_code: "4821",
            parking_notes: "driveway only",
            pet_notes: "dog in yard"
          })

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :property_path, property_path)}
      end

      when_ "a job is scheduled at that property", context do
        schedule_live = schedule_job(context.conn, context.property_path, next_week())
        {:ok, Map.put(context, :schedule_live, schedule_live)}
      end

      then_ "the job brief shows the lockbox code, parking note, and pet note from the property",
            context do
        html = render(context.schedule_live)

        assert html =~ "77 Maple Ave"
        assert html =~ "4821"
        assert html =~ "driveway only"
        assert html =~ "dog in yard"

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end

  defp create_client(conn, name) do
    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='client-form']", client: %{name: name})
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end

  defp create_property(conn, client_path, attrs) do
    "/clients/" <> client_id = client_path

    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/#{client_id}/properties/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']", property: attrs)
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end

  defp schedule_job(conn, property_path, scheduled_date) do
    "/properties/" <> property_id = property_path

    {:ok, schedule_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/schedule")

    schedule_live
    |> element("[data-test='new-job-button']")
    |> render_click()

    schedule_live
    |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
      job: %{property_id: property_id, scheduled_date: scheduled_date}
    )
    |> render_submit()

    schedule_live
  end

  defp next_week do
    Date.utc_today() |> Date.add(7) |> Date.to_iso8601()
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story833.Criterion7149Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 833 — Schedule recurring cleaning plans with series-wide conflict detection
  Criterion 7149 — A job can be assigned to a cleaner when the job's time
  does not fall inside one of that cleaner's availability blocks.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  import CleanerCrmSpex.SharedGivens

  spex "a cleaner can be assigned within their available hours" do
    scenario "assign a cleaner within their available hours" do
      given_(:logged_in_owner_with_account)

      given_ "a client \"Jamie Rivera\" with a property exists", context do
        client_path = create_client(context.conn, "Jamie Rivera")

        property_path =
          create_property(context.conn, client_path, %{service_address: "12 Oak Lane"})

        {:ok,
         Map.merge(context, %{
           client_path: client_path,
           property_id: id_from_path(property_path)
         })}
      end

      given_ "a cleaner is available Tuesday mornings", context do
        cleaner_path = create_cleaner(context.conn, "Alex Morgan")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :cleaner_id, id_from_path(cleaner_path))}
      end

      given_ "a Tuesday 9am job exists unassigned for the property", context do
        job_path =
          create_job(context.conn, %{
            property_id: context.property_id,
            date: Date.to_iso8601(next_tuesday()),
            start_time: "09:00",
            end_time: "11:00"
          })

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :job_id, id_from_path(job_path))}
      end

      when_ "the owner assigns that cleaner a Tuesday 9am job", context do
        {:ok, assign_live, _html} =
          live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule/jobs/#{context.job_id}/assign")

        assign_live
        |> form("[data-test='assignment-form']", assignment: %{cleaner_id: context.cleaner_id})
        |> render_submit()

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the job is assigned without warning", context do
        {:ok, job_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule/jobs/#{context.job_id}")

        assert has_element?(job_live, "[data-test='job-cleaner']", "Alex Morgan")
        refute html =~ "conflict"

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end

  defp id_from_path(path), do: path |> String.split("/") |> List.last()

  defp next_tuesday do
    today = Date.utc_today()
    offset = Integer.mod(2 - Date.day_of_week(today) - 1, 7) + 1
    Date.add(today, offset + 7)
  end

  defp create_client(conn, name) do
    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='client-form']", client: %{name: name})
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end

  defp create_property(conn, client_path, attrs) do
    "/clients/" <> client_id = client_path

    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/#{client_id}/properties/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']", property: attrs)
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end

  defp create_cleaner(conn, name) do
    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/schedule/cleaners/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='cleaner-form']", cleaner: %{name: name})
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end

  defp create_job(conn, attrs) do
    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/schedule/jobs/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='job-form']", job: attrs)
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Clients.Property do
  @moduledoc """
  A serviced location with address, parking, pet, and access-detail
  notes (entry method, lockbox/alarm codes, emergency contact).

  Every property belongs to exactly one client. Lockbox and alarm
  codes are stored encrypted at rest — see `CleanerCrm.Encrypted.Binary`.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  alias CleanerCrm.Encrypted

  @access_detail_fields ~w(entry_method lockbox_code alarm_code parking_notes pet_notes
                            emergency_contact_name emergency_contact_phone)a

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          service_address: String.t() | nil,
          entry_method: String.t() | nil,
          lockbox_code: String.t() | nil,
          alarm_code: String.t() | nil,
          parking_notes: String.t() | nil,
          pet_notes: String.t() | nil,
          emergency_contact_name: String.t() | nil,
          emergency_contact_phone: String.t() | nil,
          client: CleanerCrm.Clients.Client.t() | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "properties" do
    field :service_address, :string
    field :entry_method, :string
    field :lockbox_code, Encrypted.Binary
    field :alarm_code, Encrypted.Binary
    field :parking_notes, :string
    field :pet_notes, :string
    field :emergency_contact_name, :string
    field :emergency_contact_phone, :string

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @doc """
  Fields whose changes are sensitive enough to warrant an audit entry
  when updated (see `CleanerCrm.Clients.update_property/3`).
  """
  def access_code_fields, do: ~w(entry_method lockbox_code alarm_code)a

  def changeset(property, attrs) do
    property
    |> cast(blank_client_id_to_nil(attrs), [:client_id, :service_address | @access_detail_fields])
    |> validate_required([:client_id, :service_address], message: "is required")
    |> assoc_constraint(:client)
  end

  defp blank_client_id_to_nil(%{"client_id" => ""} = attrs), do: %{attrs | "client_id" => nil}
  defp blank_client_id_to_nil(attrs), do: attrs
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Clients.Client do
  @moduledoc """
  A paying customer with contact info and preferences.

  Scoped to an account: every client belongs to exactly one account and
  is only ever visible within that account.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{

          active: boolean(),
          card_on_file: boolean(),
          email: String.t() | nil,
          phone: String.t() | nil,

    field :email, :string
    field :phone, :string

    |> validate_required([:name], message: "is required")
    |> validate_length(:name, min: 1, max: 200)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story832.Criterion7117Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 832 — Manage clients and properties with access details
  Criterion 7117 — Deactivating a client with upcoming scheduled jobs
  hides it from active lists while retaining its history and
  properties.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "owner deactivates a client with upcoming jobs" do
    scenario "the deactivated client is hidden but its data is retained" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a client with a job scheduled next week", context do
        client_path = create_client(context.conn, "Morgan Reyes")

        property_path =
          create_property(context.conn, client_path, %{service_address: "9 Birch Ln"})

        schedule_job(context.conn, property_path, next_week())

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :client_path, client_path)}
      end

      when_ "the owner deactivates the client", context do
        {:ok, show_live, _html} = live(context.conn, context.client_path)

        show_live
        |> element("[data-test='deactivate-client-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the client is marked inactive and hidden from active lists", context do
        {:ok, _index_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/clients")
        refute html =~ "Morgan Reyes"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the client's history and properties are retained", context do
        {:ok, _show_live, html} = live(context.conn, context.client_path)

        assert html =~ "Morgan Reyes"
        assert html =~ "9 Birch Ln"

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end

  defp create_client(conn, name) do
    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='client-form']", client: %{name: name})
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end

  defp create_property(conn, client_path, attrs) do
    "/clients/" <> client_id = client_path

    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/#{client_id}/properties/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']", property: attrs)
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end

  defp schedule_job(conn, property_path, scheduled_date) do
    "/properties/" <> property_id = property_path

    {:ok, schedule_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/schedule")

    schedule_live
    |> element("[data-test='new-job-button']")
    |> render_click()

    schedule_live
    |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
      job: %{property_id: property_id, scheduled_date: scheduled_date}
    )
    |> render_submit()

    :ok
  end

  defp next_week do
    Date.utc_today() |> Date.add(7) |> Date.to_iso8601()
  end
end

defmodule Mix.Tasks.Spex do
  @shortdoc "Run executable specifications (spex)"
  @moduledoc """
  Run spex files - executable specifications for AI-driven development.

  SexySpex provides a framework for writing executable specifications that serve as
  both tests and living documentation, optimized for AI-driven development workflows.

  Each spex file manages its own application lifecycle using setup_all and setup blocks:
  - setup_all: Application startup and shutdown
  - setup: State reset between tests
  - Context passing between test steps
  - Integration with external tools (like ScenicMCP for GUI testing)

  ## Usage

      mix spex                    # Run all spex files
      mix spex path/to/file.exs   # Run specific spex file
      mix spex --help             # Show this help

  ## Options

      --pattern       File pattern to match (default: test/spex/**/*_spex.exs)
      --verbose       Show detailed spex Reporter output (quiet by default)
      --timeout       Test timeout in milliseconds (default: 60000)
      --manual        Interactive manual mode - step through each action
      --speed         Execution speed: fast (default), medium, slow
      --trace         Enable ExUnit trace mode (shows test execution details)
      --slowest N     Print timing information for the N slowest tests
      --formatter     ExUnit formatter module (default: ExUnit.CLIFormatter)
                      Can be specified multiple times
      --jsonl [PATH]  Output failures as JSONL (default: spex_failures.jsonl)
      --stale         Only run spex files that have changed or reference changed modules
      --force         Force all spex files to run (use with --stale to reset)

  ## Examples

      mix spex
      mix spex test/spex/user_login_spex.exs
      mix spex --pattern "**/integration_*_spex.exs"
      mix spex --verbose
      mix spex --manual           # Interactive step-by-step mode
      mix spex --speed slow       # Slower automatic execution
      mix spex --speed medium --verbose  # Medium speed with detailed output
      mix spex --trace            # Show detailed test execution
      mix spex test/spex/file.exs --trace
      mix spex --slowest 5        # Show timing for 5 slowest tests

  ## Configuration

  You can configure spex behavior in your config files:

      config :sexy_spex,
        manual_mode: false,
        step_delay: 0

  Application lifecycle is handled in individual spex files using setup_all blocks.

  ## Important: Test Environment Setup

  To ensure spex runs in the test environment with proper module compilation,
  add this to your project's mix.exs:

      def project do
        [
          # ... other config
          preferred_cli_env: [
            spex: :test
          ]
        ]
      end

  This ensures that `mix spex` always runs in the test environment and compiles
  modules with test-specific code paths (e.g., test/support directories).

  """

  use Mix.Task

  alias Mix.Compilers.Test, as: CT

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story843.Criterion7197Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 843 — Get loud, acknowledged alerts when my schedule changes
  Criterion 7197 — Office sees who has not acknowledged

  The push itself is covered end-to-end by criteria 7190/7191; this
  spec's subject is the board's acknowledgment-status visibility, so
  the already-pending notification is seeded directly via
  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.schedule_change_notification_fixture/4`.
  The scenario then re-drives the real acknowledge action on
  `FieldLive.Today` to observe the status flip on `ScheduleLive.Board`,
  since that flip is the criterion's own subject.

  Assumes the board shows a per-job acknowledgment-status control
  (`[data-test='job-<id>-ack-status']`) rendering "Unacknowledged" or
  "Acknowledged".
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "the office sees per-job acknowledgment status flip as the cleaner acknowledges" do
    scenario "office sees who has not acknowledged" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "the office pushed a schedule change to a cleaner", context do
        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "cleaner-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        cleaner_conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn(), cleaner)
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
            scheduled_date: Date.utc_today()
          })

        notification =
          Fixtures.schedule_change_notification_fixture(context.scope, cleaner, job)

        {:ok,
         Map.merge(context, %{
           cleaner: cleaner,
           cleaner_conn: cleaner_conn,
           job: job,
           notification: notification
         })}
      end

      given_ "the cleaner has not acknowledged it", context do
        {:ok, context}
      end

      when_ "the office views the change", context do
        {:ok, board_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :board_live, board_live)}
      end

      then_ "it shows as unacknowledged for that cleaner", context do
        assert has_element?(
                 context.board_live,
                 "[data-test='job-#{context.job.id}-ack-status']",
                 "Unacknowledged"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end

      when_ "the cleaner acknowledges the change", context do
        {:ok, today_live, _html} = live(context.cleaner_conn, ~p"/field")

        today_live
        |> element("[data-test='schedule-alert-#{context.notification.id}-acknowledge-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "once the cleaner acknowledges, the office sees it flip to acknowledged", context do
        {:ok, board_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        assert has_element?(
                 board_live,
                 "[data-test='job-#{context.job.id}-ack-status']",
                 "Acknowledged"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story843.Criterion7190Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 843 — Get loud, acknowledged alerts when my schedule changes
  Criterion 7190 — Moving a job's time on the schedule board pushes the
  reassigned cleaner a notification describing the old and new times.

  Assumes the board exposes a per-job start-time control
  (`[data-test='job-<id>-start-time-input']`, `phx-change="reschedule_job"`)
  alongside the cleaner-select control already assumed by story 834's
  criterion 7170.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a moved job notifies the assigned cleaner" do
    scenario "moved job notifies the cleaner" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "I am a cleaner with a job scheduled today at 1:00 PM", context do
        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "cleaner-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        cleaner_conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn(), cleaner)
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
            scheduled_date: Date.utc_today(),
            start_time: ~T[13:00:00],
            end_time: ~T[14:30:00]
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{cleaner: cleaner, cleaner_conn: cleaner_conn, job: job})}
      end

      when_ "the office moves that job to 3:00 PM", context do
        {:ok, board_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        board_live
        |> element("[data-test='job-#{context.job.id}-start-time-input']")
        |> render_change(%{"start_time" => "15:00"})

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "I receive a notification describing the change from 1:00 PM to 3:00 PM", context do
        {:ok, today_live, html} = live(context.cleaner_conn, ~p"/field")

        assert has_element?(today_live, "[data-test='schedule-alert']")
        assert html =~ "1:00 PM"
        assert html =~ "3:00 PM"

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

    end
  end

input.new_string:
# The board's own job form asks for a plain "date" — friendlier than
  # "scheduled date" — while every other caller (fixtures, other
  # contexts) uses the schema's real field name directly. A submission
  # can carry both: `Phoenix.LiveViewTest.form/3` merges an explicit
  # `scheduled_date` override on top of the form's own rendered `date`

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job do
  @moduledoc """
  A single scheduled visit: a property (or client), a time window, and
  an optional assigned cleaner.

  A job is either a one-off (`recurring_plan_id` is `nil`) or one
  occurrence materialized from a `RecurringPlan`'s cadence (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence`). Both `client_id` and
  `property_id` are independently optional at the schema level — some
  callers (time tracking, quality, notifications) only ever have a
  client on hand, while the schedule board's own job form always
  carries a property.

  ## Status

  `:scheduled` (default) -> `:in_progress` -> `:completed`, or
  `:scheduled` -> `:cancelled`. Transitions beyond create/cancel belong
  to other contexts (time tracking clocks a job into `:in_progress`).

  ## Pay fields

  `pay_type`/`hourly_rate_cents`/`piece_rate_cents` describe what the
  *cleaner* earns for this job — as distinct from `agreed_price_cents`,
  what the *client* is charged. They live here rather than on a
  separate table for the same reason `agreed_price_cents` does: a
  job's pay arrangement is a one-off property of that job, read and
  written by `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking` rather than by Scheduling
  itself.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          recurring_plan_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          scheduled_date: Date.t() | nil,
          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          status: :scheduled | :in_progress | :completed | :cancelled,
          agreed_price_cents: integer() | nil,
          pay_type: :hourly | :piece_rate | nil,
          hourly_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          piece_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "jobs" do
    field :scheduled_date, :date
    field :start_time, :time
    field :end_time, :time

    field :status, Ecto.Enum,
      values: [:scheduled, :in_progress, :completed, :cancelled],
      default: :scheduled

    field :agreed_price_cents, :integer
    field :agreed_price, :decimal, virtual: true

    field :pay_type, Ecto.Enum, values: [:hourly, :piece_rate]
    field :hourly_rate_cents, :integer
    field :piece_rate_cents, :integer

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User
    belongs_to :recurring_plan, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(client_id property_id cleaner_id recurring_plan_id scheduled_date
             start_time end_time status agreed_price_cents agreed_price
             pay_type hourly_rate_cents piece_rate_cents)a

  def changeset(job, attrs) do
    job
    |> cast(rename_date_key(attrs), @fields)
    |> validate_required([:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])
    |> validate_time_order()
    |> put_agreed_price_cents()
  end

  # The board's own job form asks for a plain "date" — friendlier than
  # "scheduled date" — while every other caller (fixtures, other
  # contexts) uses the schema's real field name directly.
  defp rename_date_key(%{"date" => date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete("date") |> Map.put("scheduled_date", date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{date: date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete(:date) |> Map.put(:scheduled_date, date)

  defp rename_date_key(attrs), do: attrs

  defp validate_time_order(changeset) do
    start_time = get_field(changeset, :start_time)
    end_time = get_field(changeset, :end_time)

    if start_time && end_time && Time.compare(start_time, end_time) != :lt do
      add_error(changeset, :end_time, "must be after the start time")
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  # `agreed_price` arrives as dollars (a `Decimal`, matching the
  # money-handling ADR's rate math); it is rounded half-up and stored
  # as `agreed_price_cents` — the only column ever persisted.
  defp put_agreed_price_cents(changeset) do
    case get_change(changeset, :agreed_price) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      %Decimal{} = amount ->
        cents = amount |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer()
        put_change(changeset, :agreed_price_cents, cents)
    end
  end
end

def cancel_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do

  @doc """
  Updates a job's schedule and/or price — a reschedule, a price
  change, or both, made directly from the board rather than through
  `assign_cleaner/3`'s conflict-checked path. Records only the fields
  that actually changed to the audit trail, attributed to the caller.
  """
  def update_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    changeset = Job.changeset(job, attrs)

    with {:ok, updated} <- Repo.update(changeset) do
      record_job_updated(scope, job, changeset, updated)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  @audited_update_fields ~w(scheduled_date start_time end_time agreed_price_cents status)a

  defp record_job_updated(scope, job, changeset, updated) do
    changed_fields =
      changeset.changes
      |> Map.keys()
      |> Enum.filter(&(&1 in @audited_update_fields))

    if changed_fields != [] do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        update_action(changed_fields),
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        audit_snapshot(job, changed_fields),
        audit_snapshot(updated, changed_fields)
      )
    end
  end

  defp update_action(changed_fields) do
    cond do
      Enum.any?(changed_fields, &(&1 in [:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])) ->
        "job_rescheduled"

      :agreed_price_cents in changed_fields ->
        "job_price_changed"

      true ->
        "job_updated"
    end
  end

  defp audit_snapshot(job, fields),
    do: Map.new(fields, &{to_string(&1), audit_value(Map.get(job, &1))})

  defp audit_value(%Date{} = value), do: to_string(value)
  defp audit_value(%Time{} = value), do: to_string(value)
  defp audit_value(value), do: value

  @doc """

  row (and any audit entries already about it) stays resolvable for
  the trail. Distinct from `cancel_job/2`: this is the office
  correcting a mistaken entry rather than calling off an appointment,
  so it's recorded as "deleted" rather than "cancelled" and never
  notifies the assigned cleaner.
  """
  def delete_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_deleted",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end
