defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling do
  @moduledoc """
  Recurring plans and the jobs they generate, cleaner time-off, and
  conflict-aware assignment.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{
    AvailabilityBlock,
    ConflictDetector,
    Job,
    Recurrence,
    RecurringPlan
  }

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  ## Jobs

  def get_job!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_job(%Scope{}, %Job{} = job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Job.changeset(job, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a job. Recorded in the audit trail as authored by the
  caller, unless `actor: :system` is passed — used when the job is one
  occurrence materialized from a recurring plan rather than a job a
  human directly asked for (see `create_recurring_plan/2`).
  """
  def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs, opts \\ [])
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, job} <-
           %Job{account_id: account_id}
           |> Job.changeset(attrs)
           |> Repo.insert() do
      record_job_created(scope, job, Keyword.get(opts, :actor, :user))
      {:ok, job}
    end
  end

  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :system) do
    Recorder.record_system(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
  end

  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :user) do
    Recorder.record(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
  end

  defp job_created_values(job) do
    %{"scheduled_date" => to_string(job.scheduled_date), "cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id}
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every job scheduled between `week_start` and six days later,
  cleaner/property/client preloaded, ordered for the board.
  """
  def list_jobs_for_week(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Date{} = week_start)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    week_end = Date.add(week_start, 6)

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date >= ^week_start and
        j.scheduled_date <= ^week_end and j.status != :cancelled
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every non-cancelled job for the account, cleaner/property/client
  preloaded, ordered for the board. Unlike `list_jobs_for_week/2`, this
  isn't bounded to a single week — a recurring plan's series can span
  months, and the board needs to account for all of it at a glance.
  """
  def list_jobs(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id and j.status != :cancelled)
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Assigns (or reassigns) a job to a cleaner, rejecting the move with
  `{:error, :unavailable}` or `{:error, :overlap}` when it conflicts
  with that cleaner's time off or an existing booking. A `nil`
  `cleaner_id` always succeeds (unassigning never conflicts).
  """
  def assign_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <-
           ConflictDetector.check_assignment(
             scope,
             cleaner_id,
             job.scheduled_date,
             job.start_time,
             job.end_time,
             exclude_job_id: job.id
           ),
         {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_reassigned",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id},
        %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def cancel_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_cancelled",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  ## Recurring plans

  def get_recurring_plan!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    RecurringPlan
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:property, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_recurring_plan(%Scope{}, %RecurringPlan{} = plan, attrs \\ %{}) do
    RecurringPlan.preview_changeset(plan, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Runs conflict detection for a (possibly unsaved) plan's full series
  against its preferred cleaner, without persisting anything. Returns
  only the conflicting occurrences, as `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
  """
  def preview_conflicts(scope, %RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
    ConflictDetector.check_occurrences(scope, plan, Recurrence.occurrences(plan))
  end

  @doc """
  Saves a recurring plan and materializes its full series of jobs.
  Conflicting occurrences are still created and still assigned to the
  preferred cleaner — conflicts are for the owner to review and
  resolve, never a silent block on saving.
  """
  def create_recurring_plan(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, plan} <-
             %RecurringPlan{account_id: account_id}
             |> RecurringPlan.changeset(attrs)
             |> Repo.insert() do
        jobs =
          plan
          |> Recurrence.job_attrs()
          |> Enum.map(fn job_attrs ->
            {:ok, job} = create_job(scope, job_attrs, actor: :system)
            job
          end)

        {:ok, {plan, jobs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  ## Availability blocks

  def change_availability_block(%Scope{}, %AvailabilityBlock{} = block, attrs \\ %{}) do
    AvailabilityBlock.changeset(block, attrs)
  end

  def create_availability_block(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %AvailabilityBlock{account_id: account_id}
    |> AvailabilityBlock.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Cleaners (account members who take jobs)

  @doc """
  Lists the account's members as candidate cleaners for the board and
  assignment pickers.
  """
  def list_cleaners(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> Accounts.list_account_members(account_id)
    |> Enum.map(& &1.user)
  end

  @doc """
  Registers a new cleaner: a user identified by display name (rather
  than login credentials) added to the account as a member, so jobs
  and availability can be assigned to them. There is no login flow for
  a cleaner created this way — see `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3`
  for the (real, login-capable) path other stories seed cleaners
  through.
  """
  def register_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, name)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(name) do
    with {:ok, user} <- insert_cleaner_user(name),
         {:ok, _member} <- Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account_id, :member) do
      {:ok, user}
    end
  end

  defp insert_cleaner_user(name) do
    %User{}
    |> Ecto.Changeset.cast(%{name: name, email: placeholder_email(name)}, [:name, :email])
    |> Ecto.Changeset.validate_required([:name, :email])
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp placeholder_email(name) do
    slug =
      name
      |> String.downcase()
      |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]+/, ".")
      |> String.trim(".")

    "#{slug}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@cleaners.local"
  end
end

# The board's own job form asks for a plain "date" — friendlier than
  # "scheduled date" — while every other caller (fixtures, other
  # contexts) uses the schema's real field name directly. A submission
  # can carry both: `Phoenix.LiveViewTest.form/3` merges an explicit
  # `scheduled_date` override on top of the form's own rendered `date`
  # default rather than replacing it, so an explicit `scheduled_date`
  # always wins and the stray `date` is dropped.
  defp rename_date_key(%{"scheduled_date" => _} = attrs), do: Map.delete(attrs, "date")
  defp rename_date_key(%{scheduled_date: _} = attrs), do: Map.delete(attrs, :date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{"date" => date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete("date") |> Map.put("scheduled_date", date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{date: date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete(:date) |> Map.put(:scheduled_date, date)

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job do
  @moduledoc """
  A single scheduled visit: a property (or client), a time window, and
  an optional assigned cleaner.

  A job is either a one-off (`recurring_plan_id` is `nil`) or one
  occurrence materialized from a `RecurringPlan`'s cadence (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence`). Both `client_id` and
  `property_id` are independently optional at the schema level — some
  callers (time tracking, quality, notifications) only ever have a
  client on hand, while the schedule board's own job form always
  carries a property.

  ## Status

  `:scheduled` (default) -> `:in_progress` -> `:completed`, or
  `:scheduled` -> `:cancelled`. Transitions beyond create/cancel belong
  to other contexts (time tracking clocks a job into `:in_progress`).

  ## Pay fields

  `pay_type`/`hourly_rate_cents`/`piece_rate_cents` describe what the
  *cleaner* earns for this job — as distinct from `agreed_price_cents`,
  what the *client* is charged. They live here rather than on a
  separate table for the same reason `agreed_price_cents` does: a
  job's pay arrangement is a one-off property of that job, read and
  written by `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking` rather than by Scheduling
  itself.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          recurring_plan_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          scheduled_date: Date.t() | nil,
          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          status: :scheduled | :in_progress | :completed | :cancelled,
          agreed_price_cents: integer() | nil,
          pay_type: :hourly | :piece_rate | nil,
          hourly_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          piece_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "jobs" do
    field :scheduled_date, :date
    field :start_time, :time
    field :end_time, :time

    field :status, Ecto.Enum,
      values: [:scheduled, :in_progress, :completed, :cancelled],
      default: :scheduled

    field :agreed_price_cents, :integer
    field :agreed_price, :decimal, virtual: true

    field :pay_type, Ecto.Enum, values: [:hourly, :piece_rate]
    field :hourly_rate_cents, :integer
    field :piece_rate_cents, :integer

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User
    belongs_to :recurring_plan, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(client_id property_id cleaner_id recurring_plan_id scheduled_date
             start_time end_time status agreed_price_cents agreed_price
             pay_type hourly_rate_cents piece_rate_cents)a

  def changeset(job, attrs) do
    job
    |> cast(rename_date_key(attrs), @fields)
    |> validate_required([:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])
    |> validate_time_order()
    |> put_agreed_price_cents()
  end

  # The board's own job form asks for a plain "date" — friendlier than
  # "scheduled date" — while every other caller (fixtures, other
  # contexts) uses the schema's real field name directly. A submission
  # can carry both: `Phoenix.LiveViewTest.form/3` merges an explicit
  # `scheduled_date` override on top of the form's own rendered `date`
  # default rather than replacing it, so an explicit `scheduled_date`
  # always wins and the stray `date` is dropped.
  defp rename_date_key(%{"scheduled_date" => _} = attrs), do: Map.delete(attrs, "date")
  defp rename_date_key(%{scheduled_date: _} = attrs), do: Map.delete(attrs, :date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{"date" => date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete("date") |> Map.put("scheduled_date", date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{date: date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete(:date) |> Map.put(:scheduled_date, date)

  defp rename_date_key(attrs), do: attrs

  defp validate_time_order(changeset) do
    start_time = get_field(changeset, :start_time)
    end_time = get_field(changeset, :end_time)

    if start_time && end_time && Time.compare(start_time, end_time) != :lt do
      add_error(changeset, :end_time, "must be after the start time")
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  # `agreed_price` arrives as dollars (a `Decimal`, matching the
  # money-handling ADR's rate math); it is rounded half-up and stored
  # as `agreed_price_cents` — the only column ever persisted.
  defp put_agreed_price_cents(changeset) do
    case get_change(changeset, :agreed_price) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      %Decimal{} = amount ->
        cents = amount |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer()
        put_change(changeset, :agreed_price_cents, cents)
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story840.Criterion7204Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 840 — See an audit trail of schedule and record changes
  Criterion 7204 — Automated recurring job generation is attributed to
  the system: Dana authors the recurring plan, but the individual job
  occurrences it materializes are created by an automated process with
  no human involved, so each of those audit entries must name the
  system as actor rather than Dana or a blank author.

  Assumes `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.PlanFormComponent` (opened from
  `/schedule/plans/new`, per story 833's own specs) exposes a
  `[data-test='plan-form']` (submitted via `render_change`) and a
  `[data-test='save-plan-button']` that saves the plan and, per
  criterion 7143, materializes its job occurrences immediately.
  Assumes `CleanerCrmWeb.AuditLive` (`/audit`) renders one entry per
  materialized job and names its actor "System" when no human made the
  change.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "automated recurring job generation is attributed to the system" do
    scenario "jobs materialized by a saved weekly plan are logged as system-authored" do
      given_ "office staffer Dana is logged in with an active account", context do
        user =
          Fixtures.user_fixture(%{
            email: "dana-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a client's property and an available cleaner exist", context do
        client_path = create_client(context.conn, "Riverside HOA")

        property_path =
          create_property(context.conn, client_path, %{service_address: "9 River Rd"})

        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "sam-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{property_id: id_from_path(property_path), cleaner: cleaner})}
      end

      when_ "Dana creates a weekly recurring plan for that property", context do
        {:ok, plan_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule/plans/new")

        plan_live
        |> form("[data-test='plan-form']",
          plan: %{
            property_id: context.property_id,
            cleaner_id: context.cleaner.id,
            recurrence: "weekly",
            start_date: Date.to_iso8601(first_visit_date()),
            occurrence_count: 3
          }
        )
        |> render_change()

        plan_live
        |> element("[data-test='save-plan-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the audit trail attributes every materialized job to the System, not Dana",
            context do
        {:ok, _audit_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/audit")

        assert html =~ "Riverside HOA"
        assert length(Regex.scan(~r/System/, html)) >= 3

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end

  defp first_visit_date, do: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 14)
  defp id_from_path(path), do: path |> String.split("/") |> List.last()

  defp create_client(conn, name) do
    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='client-form']", client: %{name: name})
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end

  defp create_property(conn, client_path, attrs) do
    "/clients/" <> client_id = client_path

    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/#{client_id}/properties/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']", property: attrs)
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end
end

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "automated recurring job generation is attributed to the system" do
    scenario "jobs materialized by a saved weekly plan are logged as system-authored" do
      given_ "office staffer Dana is logged in with an active account", context do
        user =
          Fixtures.user_fixture(%{
            email: "dana-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a client's property and an available cleaner exist", context do
        client_path = create_client(context.conn, "Riverside HOA")

        property_path =
          create_property(context.conn, client_path, %{service_address: "9 River Rd"})

        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "sam-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{property_id: id_from_path(property_path), cleaner: cleaner})}
      end

      when_ "Dana creates a weekly recurring plan for that property", context do
        {:ok, plan_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule/plans/new")

        plan_live
        |> form("[data-test='plan-form']",
          plan: %{
            property_id: context.property_id,
            cleaner_id: context.cleaner.id,
            recurrence: "weekly",
            start_date: Date.to_iso8601(first_visit_date()),
            occurrence_count: 3
          }
        )
        |> render_change()

        plan_live
        |> element("[data-test='save-plan-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the audit trail attributes every materialized job to the System, not Dana",
            context do
        {:ok, _audit_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/audit")

        assert html =~ "Riverside HOA"
        assert length(Regex.scan(~r/System/, html)) >= 3

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end

  defp first_visit_date, do: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 14)
  defp id_from_path(path), do: path |> String.split("/") |> List.last()

  defp create_client(conn, name) do
    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='client-form']", client: %{name: name})
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end

  defp create_property(conn, client_path, attrs) do
    "/clients/" <> client_id = client_path

    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/#{client_id}/properties/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']", property: attrs)
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end
end

@doc """
  Creates a job. Recorded in the audit trail as authored by the
  caller, unless `actor: :system` is passed — used when the job is one
  occurrence materialized from a recurring plan rather than a job a
  human directly asked for (see `create_recurring_plan/2`).
  """
  def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs, opts \\ [])
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, job} <-
           %Job{account_id: account_id}
           |> Job.changeset(attrs)
           |> Repo.insert() do
      record_job_created(scope, job, Keyword.get(opts, :actor, :user))
      {:ok, job}
    end
  end

  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :system) do
    Recorder.record_system(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
  end

  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :user) do
    Recorder.record(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
  end

  defp job_created_values(job) do
    %{"scheduled_date" => to_string(job.scheduled_date), "cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id}
  end

  @doc """

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story837.Criterion7187Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 837 — Send automated appointment reminders to clients
  Criterion 7187 — Client confirms the appointment

  The reminder send itself is covered end-to-end by criterion 7183;
  this spec's subject is the confirm action's effect, so the
  already-sent reminder is seeded directly via
  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.notification_fixture/4`.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "confirming via the reminder marks the appointment confirmed" do
    scenario "client confirms the appointment" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a client received a reminder for an unconfirmed appointment", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{name: "Priya Nair"})
        job = Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{status: :scheduled})
        notification = Fixtures.notification_fixture(context.scope, client, job)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, job: job, notification: notification})}
      end

      when_ "the client taps confirm", context do
        confirm_conn =
          Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn()
          |> get(~p"/reminders/confirm/#{context.notification.token}")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :confirm_conn, confirm_conn)}
      end

      then_ "the appointment is marked confirmed for the client", context do
        assert Phoenix.ConnTest.html_response(context.confirm_conn, 200) =~ "Confirmed"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the owner sees it as confirmed on the schedule board", context do
        {:ok, board_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        assert has_element?(board_live, "[data-test='job-#{context.job.id}']", "Confirmed")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story837.Criterion7188Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 837 — Send automated appointment reminders to clients
  Criterion 7188 — Client requests a reschedule

  As in criterion 7187, the reminder is seeded directly via
  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.notification_fixture/4` since sending it
  is covered end-to-end by criterion 7183; this spec's subject is the
  reschedule action's effect.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "requesting reschedule via the reminder flags the appointment and notifies the owner" do
    scenario "client requests a reschedule" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a client received a reminder for an upcoming appointment", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{name: "Sam Okafor"})
        job = Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{status: :scheduled})
        notification = Fixtures.notification_fixture(context.scope, client, job)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, job: job, notification: notification})}
      end

      when_ "the client taps reschedule", context do
        reschedule_conn =
          Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn()
          |> get(~p"/reminders/reschedule/#{context.notification.token}")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :reschedule_conn, reschedule_conn)}
      end

      then_ "the appointment is flagged for reschedule", context do
        assert Phoenix.ConnTest.html_response(context.reschedule_conn, 200) =~
                 "Reschedule requested"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the owner is notified to rebook it, protecting route density", context do
        {:ok, board_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        assert has_element?(board_live, "[data-test='job-#{context.job.id}']", "Needs reschedule")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications do
  @moduledoc """
  Client appointment reminders with confirm/reschedule actions, and
  cleaner schedule-change alerts requiring explicit acknowledgment with
  office visibility into what's still unacknowledged. Email/SMS
  delivery is abstracted behind `CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery`.

  Most functions are scoped by the caller's `Scope`. The confirm,
  reschedule, and delivery-status webhook endpoints are reached by an
  unauthenticated client or provider, so they look a notification up by
  its opaque `token` (or the provider's message id) instead.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications.{
    Notification,
    ReminderNotifier,
    ReminderScheduler,
    ReminderSettings
  }

  ## Reminder settings

  @doc "The account's reminder settings, defaulting to a 24-hour lead time if never configured."
  def get_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(ReminderSettings, account_id: account_id) do
      nil -> %ReminderSettings{account_id: account_id}
      settings -> settings
    end
  end

  def change_reminder_settings(%Scope{} = scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope |> get_reminder_settings() |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
  end

  def update_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> get_reminder_settings()
    |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert_or_update()
  end

  @doc "Runs the periodic reminder scan now — see `CleanerCrm.Notifications.ReminderScheduler`."
  defdelegate send_due_reminders(), to: ReminderScheduler, as: :scan_and_send

  ## Notifications

  def create_notification(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Notification{account_id: account_id}
    |> Notification.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc "The office's delivery log: every notification for the account, most recent first."
  def list_notifications(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)
    |> preload([:client, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Public confirm/reschedule — reached by token, no scope available

  def get_notification_by_token(token) when is_binary(token) do
    Repo.get_by(Notification, token: token)
  end

  def confirm_reminder(token) when is_binary(token) do
    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
      update_status(notification, status: :confirmed, confirmed_at: DateTime.utc_now())
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
    end
  end

  def request_reschedule(token) when is_binary(token) do
    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
      update_status(notification,
        status: :reschedule_requested,
        reschedule_requested_at: DateTime.utc_now()
      )
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
    end
  end

  @doc "True once the client has confirmed the most recent reminder sent for this job."
  def job_confirmed?(job_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder and n.status == :confirmed)
    |> Repo.exists?()
  end

  @doc "True once the client has asked to reschedule via the most recent reminder for this job."
  def reschedule_requested?(job_id) do
    Notification
    |> where(
      [n],
      n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder and n.status == :reschedule_requested
    )
    |> Repo.exists?()
  end

  @doc """
  The client's confirm/reschedule decision on their most recent
  reminder for this job, for `ScheduleLive.Index` to render on the
  board — `nil` (no decision yet), `:confirmed`, or
  `:reschedule_requested`.
  """
  def reminder_status_for_job(job_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder)
    |> where([n], n.status in [:confirmed, :reschedule_requested])
    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> select([n], n.status)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  ## Twilio delivery-status webhook

  @doc """
  Applies a Twilio status callback: marks the matching notification
  delivered or undelivered, and — for an undeliverable SMS reminder —
  falls back to emailing the client and flags it for office visibility.
  """
  def handle_delivery_status(%{"MessageSid" => sid, "MessageStatus" => status} = params)
      when is_binary(sid) do
    case Repo.get_by(Notification, provider_message_id: sid) do
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
      notification -> apply_delivery_status(notification, status, params["ErrorCode"])
    end
  end

  def handle_delivery_status(_params), do: {:error, :invalid_payload}

  defp apply_delivery_status(notification, "delivered", _error_code) do
    update_status(notification, status: :delivered, delivered_at: DateTime.utc_now())
  end

  defp apply_delivery_status(notification, status, error_code)
       when status in ["failed", "undelivered"] do
    with {:ok, updated} <-
           update_status(notification, status: :undelivered, failure_reason: error_code || status) do
      maybe_fallback_to_email(updated)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  defp apply_delivery_status(notification, _status, _error_code), do: {:ok, notification}

  defp maybe_fallback_to_email(
         %Notification{kind: :reminder, channel: :sms, client_id: client_id} = notification
       )
       when not is_nil(client_id) do
    client = Repo.get!(CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, notification.client_id)
    job = Repo.get!(CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, notification.job_id)
    token = generate_token()

    confirm_url = reminder_url("/reminders/confirm/#{token}")
    reschedule_url = reminder_url("/reminders/reschedule/#{token}")

    {:ok, _email} = ReminderNotifier.deliver_reminder(client, job, confirm_url, reschedule_url)

    %Notification{account_id: notification.account_id}
    |> Notification.changeset(%{
      client_id: client.id,
      job_id: job.id,
      kind: :reminder,
      channel: :email,
      status: :sent,
      token: token,
      sent_at: DateTime.utc_now()
    })
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp maybe_fallback_to_email(_notification), do: :ok

  ## Schedule-change alerts (story 843 groundwork)

  def acknowledge(token) when is_binary(token) do
    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
      update_status(notification, status: :acknowledged, acknowledged_at: DateTime.utc_now())
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
    end
  end

  @doc "Pending schedule-change alerts a cleaner hasn't acknowledged yet, for office visibility."
  def list_unacknowledged(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where(
      [n],
      n.account_id == ^account_id and n.kind == :schedule_change and n.status == :pending
    )
    |> preload([:cleaner, :job])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  The most recent schedule-change alert pushed for this job — `nil`,
  or a `Notification` exposing `:status`
  (`:pending` | `:acknowledged` | `:escalated`) and `:channel`
  (`:push` | `:sms` | `:email`). This is the contract
  `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.Index` reads defensively to show a job's
  ack status on the board.
  """
  def latest_schedule_change_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, job_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where(
      [n],
      n.account_id == ^account_id and n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :schedule_change
    )
    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  ## Shared helpers

  @doc false
  def generate_token, do: Base.url_encode64(:crypto.strong_rand_bytes(24), padding: false)

  defp update_status(%Notification{} = notification, attrs) do
    notification
    |> Notification.changeset(Map.new(attrs))
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  # `CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url()` is the standard phx.gen.auth-style
  # exception for building absolute links in outbound messages — see
  # the `dirty_xrefs` note on the `CleanerCrm` boundary.
  defp reminder_url(path), do: CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url() <> path
end

Unassigned

  defp ack_status_label(%{status: :escalated}), do: "Escalated"

# `CleanerCrm.Notifications` owns the per-job schedule-change alert
  # (acknowledgment status, fallback channel) and the client's
  # reminder confirm/reschedule decision. Read both defensively —
  # `function_exported?` rather than a direct call — so this file
  # tolerates that context landing or changing shape independently of
  # the board.
  defp notifications_ready?(fun, arity),
    do:
      Code.ensure_loaded?(CleanerCrm.Notifications) and
        function_exported?(CleanerCrm.Notifications, fun, arity)

  # Expected contract: `latest_schedule_change_for_job(scope, job_id)`
  # returns `nil` or something map-like with `:status`
  # (`:pending` | `:acknowledged` | `:escalated`) and `:channel`
  # (`:push` | `:sms` | `:email`) keys, matching
  # `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.schedule_change_notification_fixture/4`'s
  # shape.
  defp schedule_change_alert(scope, job) do
    if notifications_ready?(:latest_schedule_change_for_job, 2) do
      CleanerCrm.Notifications.latest_schedule_change_for_job(scope, job.id)
    end
  end

  defp ack_status_label(%{status: :pending}), do: "Unacknowledged"
  defp ack_status_label(%{status: :acknowledged}), do: "Acknowledged"
  defp ack_status_label(%{status: :escalated}), do: "Escalated"
  defp ack_status_label(_alert), do: "Unacknowledged"

  defp channel_label(%{channel: :push}), do: "Push"
  defp channel_label(%{channel: :sms}), do: "SMS"
  defp channel_label(%{channel: :email}), do: "Email"
  defp channel_label(_alert), do: "Push"

  # Expected contract: `reminder_status_for_job(job_id)` returns `nil`
  # (no decision yet), `:confirmed`, or `:reschedule_requested` — the
  # client's most recent decision on their appointment reminder.
  defp reminder_status(job) do
    if notifications_ready?(:reminder_status_for_job, 1) do
      CleanerCrm.Notifications.reminder_status_for_job(job.id)
    end
  end

  defp reminder_status_label(:confirmed), do: "Confirmed"
  defp reminder_status_label(:reschedule_requested), do: "Needs reschedule"
  defp reminder_status_label(_status), do: nil
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story843.Criterion7203Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 843 — Get loud, acknowledged alerts when my schedule changes
  Criterion 7203 — Push failure falls back to SMS

  "My push notification cannot be delivered" is modeled as the cleaner
  having no push channel registered (`push_enabled: false`) — there is
  no push-registration flow anywhere in this app, so a cleaner who has
  never enabled push is the natural, real-world precondition rather
  than a fabricated delivery-status callback. "The system sends the
  change" re-drives the same real trigger as criterion 7190 (moving a
  job on `ScheduleLive.Board`); the fallback is observed via the
  board's per-job notification-channel control
  (`[data-test='job-<id>-notification-channel']`), never a live
  Twilio call.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a schedule change falls back to SMS when push cannot be delivered" do
    scenario "push failure falls back to SMS" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a schedule change needs to reach me", context do
        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "cleaner-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com",
            push_enabled: false
          })

        cleaner_conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn(), cleaner)
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
            scheduled_date: Date.utc_today(),
            start_time: ~T[13:00:00],
            end_time: ~T[14:30:00]
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{cleaner: cleaner, cleaner_conn: cleaner_conn, job: job})}
      end

      given_ "my push notification cannot be delivered", context do
        {:ok, context}
      end

      when_ "the system sends the change", context do
        {:ok, board_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        board_live
        |> element("[data-test='job-#{context.job.id}-start-time-input']")
        |> render_change(%{"start_time" => "15:00"})

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "it falls back to sending me an SMS with the change details", context do
        {:ok, board_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        assert has_element?(
                 board_live,
                 "[data-test='job-#{context.job.id}-notification-channel']",
                 "SMS"
               )

        assert has_element?(
                 board_live,
                 "[data-test='job-#{context.job.id}-notification-channel']",
                 "3:00 PM"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

defmodule CleanerCrm.Users.User do
  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  schema "users" do
    field :email, :string
    field :name, :string
    field :password, :string, virtual: true, redact: true
    field :hashed_password, :string, redact: true
    field :confirmed_at, :utc_datetime
    field :authenticated_at, :utc_datetime, virtual: true

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime)
  end

  @doc """
  A user changeset for registering or changing the email.

  It requires the email to change otherwise an error is added.

  ## Options

    * `:validate_unique` - Set to false if you don't want to validate the
      uniqueness of the email, useful when displaying live validations.
      Defaults to `true`.
  """
  def email_changeset(user, attrs, opts \\ []) do
    user
    |> cast(attrs, [:email])
    |> validate_email(opts)
  end

  defp validate_email(changeset, opts) do
    changeset =
      changeset
      |> validate_required([:email])
      |> validate_format(:email, ~r/^[^@,;\s]+@[^@,;\s]+$/,
        message: "must have the @ sign and no spaces"
      )
      |> validate_length(:email, max: 160)

    if Keyword.get(opts, :validate_unique, true) do
      changeset
      |> unsafe_validate_unique(:email, CleanerCrm.Repo)
      |> unique_constraint(:email)
      |> validate_email_changed()
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  defp validate_email_changed(changeset) do
    if get_field(changeset, :email) && get_change(changeset, :email) == nil do
      add_error(changeset, :email, "did not change")
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  @doc """

defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications.Notification do
  @moduledoc """
  An outbound message — a client appointment reminder or a cleaner
  schedule-change alert — with delivery status and acknowledgment
  tracking.

  `kind: :reminder` notifications carry a `client_id` and move through
  `:sent -> :delivered | :undelivered -> :confirmed | :reschedule_requested`.
  `kind: :schedule_change` notifications carry a `cleaner_id` instead
  and move through `:pending -> :acknowledged` (or `:escalated` when
  never acknowledged in time).
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @kinds [:reminder, :schedule_change]
  @channels [:email, :sms, :push]
  @statuses [
    :pending,
    :sent,
    :delivered,
    :undelivered,
    :failed,
    :confirmed,
    :reschedule_requested,
    :acknowledged,
    :escalated
  ]

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          job_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          kind: :reminder | :schedule_change,
          channel: :email | :sms | :push,
          status: atom(),
          token: String.t() | nil,
          provider_message_id: String.t() | nil,
          failure_reason: String.t() | nil,
          change_summary: String.t() | nil,
          pushed_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          sent_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          delivered_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          confirmed_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          reschedule_requested_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          acknowledged_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          escalated_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "notifications" do
    field :kind, Ecto.Enum, values: @kinds
    field :channel, Ecto.Enum, values: @channels
    field :status, Ecto.Enum, values: @statuses, default: :pending
    field :token, :string
    field :provider_message_id, :string
    field :failure_reason, :string
    field :change_summary, :string

    field :pushed_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :sent_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :delivered_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :confirmed_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :reschedule_requested_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :acknowledged_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :escalated_at, :utc_datetime_usec

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User
    belongs_to :job, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(client_id cleaner_id job_id kind channel status token provider_message_id
             failure_reason change_summary pushed_at sent_at delivered_at confirmed_at
             reschedule_requested_at acknowledged_at escalated_at)a

  def changeset(notification, attrs) do
    notification
    |> cast(attrs, @fields)
    |> validate_required([:job_id, :kind, :channel, :token])
    |> unique_constraint(:token)
    |> foreign_key_constraint(:job_id)

  # or cancellation. This is the sanctioned place for it, not
  # `CleanerCrm.Scheduling`: the dependency graph has
  # `Notifications -> Scheduling`, so `Scheduling` itself must never
  # call back into `Notifications` — this LiveView is what's allowed
  # to depend on both and compose them. No-ops for an unassigned job
  # (nobody to notify) or if `Notifications` isn't loaded yet.
  defp notify_schedule_change(scope, job, change_summary) do
    if job.cleaner_id && notifications_ready?(:create_notification, 2) do
      cleaner = Enum.find(Scheduling.list_cleaners(scope), &(&1.id == job.cleaner_id))

      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(scope, %{

  defp notification_channel(%{push_enabled: false}), do: :sms
  defp notification_channel(_cleaner), do: :push

  defp to_12_hour(12), do: {12, "PM"}
  defp to_12_hour(hour), do: {hour - 12, "PM"}
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story846.Criterion7196Spex do

  "records the client's preferred cleaner" per its architecture spec —
  and a `[data-test='save-plan-button']` that saves the plan and
  materializes its occurrence(s) immediately, per criterion 7143.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  import CleanerCrmSpex.SharedGivens

  spex "the owner designates a preferred cleaner when creating a recurring plan" do
    scenario "owner sets a preferred cleaner on a recurring plan" do
      given_(:logged_in_owner_with_account)

      given_ "a client \"Jamie Rivera\" with a property exists", context do
        client_path = create_client(context.conn, "Jamie Rivera")

        property_path =
          create_property(context.conn, client_path, %{service_address: "12 Oak Lane"})

        {:ok,
         Map.merge(context, %{
           client_path: client_path,
           property_id: id_from_path(property_path)
         })}
      end

      given_ "a cleaner \"Alex Morgan\" is available for assignment", context do
        cleaner_path = create_cleaner(context.conn, "Alex Morgan")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :cleaner_id, id_from_path(cleaner_path))}
      end

      when_ "the owner creates a recurring plan and sets Alex Morgan as the preferred cleaner",
            context do
        {:ok, plan_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule/plans/new")

        plan_live
        |> form("[data-test='plan-form']",
          plan: %{
            property_id: context.property_id,
            cleaner_id: context.cleaner_id,
            recurrence: "weekly",
            start_date: Date.to_iso8601(first_visit_date()),
            occurrence_count: 1
          }
        )
        |> render_change()

        plan_live
        |> element("[data-test='save-plan-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the plan's generated visit is assigned to the preferred cleaner, Alex Morgan",
            context do
        {:ok, board_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        [job_id] = job_ids(html)

        assert has_element?(
                 board_live,
                 "[data-test='cleaner-column-#{context.cleaner_id}'] [data-test='job-#{job_id}']"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end

  defp first_visit_date, do: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 14)
  defp id_from_path(path), do: path |> String.split("/") |> List.last()

  defp job_ids(html) do
    ~r/data-test="job-(\d+)"/
    |> Regex.scan(html)
    |> Enum.map(fn [_, id] -> id end)
    |> Enum.uniq()
  end

  defp create_client(conn, name) do
    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='client-form']", client: %{name: name})
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end

  defp create_property(conn, client_path, attrs) do
    "/clients/" <> client_id = client_path

    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/#{client_id}/properties/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']", property: attrs)
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end

  defp create_cleaner(conn, name) do
    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/schedule/cleaners/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='cleaner-form']", cleaner: %{name: name})
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan do
  @moduledoc """
  A weekly/biweekly/monthly cadence for a property that materializes a
  series of `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job` rows (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence`).

  `cleaner_id` is the client's *preferred* cleaner (story 846): every
  job generated from this plan defaults to this cleaner, and
  reassigning a single visit away from them is a warning, not a block.
  It is optional — a plan with no preferred cleaner generates
  unassigned jobs and never warns on reassignment.

  `start_time`/`end_time` default to a plain 9am-11am visit window;
  nothing in the plan form asks for these explicitly today, but every
  generated job needs a concrete time to run conflict detection
  against.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          recurrence: :weekly | :biweekly | :monthly | nil,
          start_date: Date.t() | nil,
          occurrence_count: integer() | nil,
          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "recurring_plans" do
    field :recurrence, Ecto.Enum, values: [:weekly, :biweekly, :monthly]
    field :start_date, :date
    field :occurrence_count, :integer
    field :start_time, :time, default: ~T[09:00:00]
    field :end_time, :time, default: ~T[11:00:00]

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(property_id cleaner_id recurrence start_date occurrence_count start_time end_time)a

  @doc """
  Changeset for the fully-specified plan a save requires.
  """
  def changeset(plan, attrs) do
    plan
    |> cast(attrs, @fields)
    |> validate_required([:property_id, :recurrence, :start_date, :occurrence_count])
    |> validate_number(:occurrence_count, greater_than: 0)
  end

  @doc """
  Changeset for the live preview as the owner fills in the form —
  every field is optional so the conflict list can update incrementally
  as soon as enough of them are present, well before the plan is valid
  enough to save.
  """
  def preview_changeset(plan, attrs) do
    cast(plan, attrs, @fields)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence do
  @moduledoc """
  Generates the dates for a plan's series from its cadence.

  Project-local, calendar-date arithmetic (see the recurrence ADR) —
  no RRULE library, no virtual occurrences. `:weekly` steps 7 days,
  `:biweekly` 14, `:monthly` 28 (a fixed 4-week cadence, not a calendar
  month, so the weekday never drifts).

  TODO: the recurrence ADR calls for materializing against each
  account's IANA timezone (via `tzdata`) so visits stay pinned to local
  wall-clock across DST, plus a rolling 12-week horizon extended by a
  daily Oban job. Neither is implemented yet — dates here are naive
  and every plan is materialized in full up front, bounded only by its
  own `occurrence_count`.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan

  @step_days %{weekly: 7, biweekly: 14, monthly: 28}

  @doc """
  Returns a list of `%{index:, date:}` maps, one per occurrence, in
  series order starting at 1. `nil` if the plan is missing any of the
  fields a series needs.
  """
  def occurrences(%RecurringPlan{
        recurrence: recurrence,
        start_date: %Date{} = start_date,
        occurrence_count: count
      })
      when recurrence in [:weekly, :biweekly, :monthly] and is_integer(count) and count > 0 do
    step = Map.fetch!(@step_days, recurrence)

    for index <- 1..count do
      %{index: index, date: Date.add(start_date, (index - 1) * step)}
    end
  end

  def occurrences(_incomplete_plan), do: []

  @doc """
  Job attribute maps ready for `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.create_job/2`, one
  per occurrence.
  """
  def job_attrs(%RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
    Enum.map(occurrences(plan), fn %{date: date} ->
      %{
        property_id: plan.property_id,
        cleaner_id: plan.cleaner_id,
        recurring_plan_id: plan.id,
        scheduled_date: date,
        start_time: plan.start_time,
        end_time: plan.end_time
      }
    end)
  end
end

107 108
109 """ 110 end 111 112 @impl true 113 def update(%{plan: plan} = assigns, socket) do 114 changeset = Scheduling.change_recurring_plan(assigns.current_scope, plan, %{}) 115 116 {:ok, 117 socket 118 |> assign(assigns) 119 |> assign(:overridden, MapSet.new()) 120 |> assign(:properties, list_properties(assigns.current_scope)) 121 |> assign(:cleaners, Scheduling.list_cleaners(assigns.current_scope)) 122 |> assign_form_and_conflicts(changeset)} 123 end 124 125 @impl true 126 def handle_event("validate", %{"plan" => params}, socket) do 127 changeset = 128 socket.assigns.current_scope 129 |> Scheduling.change_recurring_plan(socket.assigns.plan, params) 130 |> Map.put(:action, :validate) 131 132 {:noreply, assign_form_and_conflicts(socket, changeset)} 133 end 134 135 def handle_event("override_conflict", %{"index" => index}, socket) do 136 index = String.to_integer(index) 137 138 {:noreply, 139 socket 140 |> Phoenix.Component.update(:overridden, &MapSet.put(&1, index)) 141 |> Phoenix.Component.update( 142 :conflicts, 143 &Enum.reject(&1, fn conflict -> conflict.index == index end) 144 )} 145 end 146 147 # The save button is a plain `phx-click`, not a form submit — the 148 # board's own conflict-review flow drives it that way (see the 149 # spex). It carries no params of its own, so it saves whatever the 150 # last "validate" pass put in the form. 151 def handle_event("save", %{"plan" => params}, socket), do: save_plan(socket, params) 152 153 def handle_event("save", _params, socket), 154 do: save_plan(socket, socket.assigns.form.params || %{}) 155 156 defp save_plan(socket, params) do 157 case Scheduling.create_recurring_plan(socket.assigns.current_scope, params) do 158 {:ok, {plan, _jobs}} -> 159 notify_parent({:saved, plan}) 160 changeset = Scheduling.change_recurring_plan(socket.assigns.current_scope, plan, %{}) 161 162 {:noreply, 163 socket 164 |> assign(:plan, plan) 165 |> assign_form_and_conflicts(changeset)} 166 167 {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} -> 168 {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset, as: :plan))} 169 end 170 end 171 172 defp assign_form_and_conflicts(socket, changeset) do 173 draft = Ecto.Changeset.apply_changes(changeset) 174 175 conflicts = 176 socket.assigns.current_scope 177 |> Scheduling.preview_conflicts(draft) 178 |> Enum.reject(&MapSet.member?(socket.assigns.overridden, &1.index)) 179 180 socket 181 |> assign(:form, to_form(changeset, as: :plan)) 182 |> assign(:conflicts, conflicts) 183 end 184 185 defp notify_parent(msg), do: send(self(), {__MODULE__, msg}) 186 187 defp list_properties(%{active_account_id: account_id}) do 188 Property 189 |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id) 190 |> order_by([p], asc: p.service_address) 191 |> Repo.all() 192 end 193 194 defp property_options(properties), do: Enum.map(properties, &{&1.service_address, &1.id}) 195 defp cleaner_options(cleaners), do: Enum.map(cleaners, &{&1.name || &1.email, &1.id}) 196 197 defp conflict_reason_text(:unavailable), do: "the cleaner is unavailable that day" 198 defp conflict_reason_text(:overlap), do: "it overlaps another booking" 199 200 defp form_title(:new), do: "New Recurring Plan" 201 defp form_title(:edit), do: "Edit Recurring Plan" 202 end 203

<.header>{form_title(@action)} <.form for={@form} id={"#{@id}-form"} data-test="plan-form" phx-target={@myself} phx-change="validate" phx-submit="save" > <.input field={@form[:property_id]} type="select" label="Property" prompt="Select a property" options={property_options(@properties)} /> <.input field={@form[:cleaner_id]} type="select" label="Preferred Cleaner" prompt="No preferred cleaner" options={cleaner_options(@cleaners)} /> <.input field={@form[:recurrence]} type="select" label="Recurrence" prompt="Select a cadence" options={[{"Weekly", "weekly"}, {"Biweekly", "biweekly"}, {"Every 4 weeks", "monthly"}]} /> <.input field={@form[:start_date]} type="date" label="Start Date" /> <.input field={@form[:occurrence_count]} type="number" label="Number of Visits" min="1" />
Visit {conflict.index} ({conflict.date}) has a scheduling conflict: {conflict_reason_text( conflict.reason )}. <.button type="button" data-test={"override-conflict-#{conflict.index}"} phx-target={@myself} phx-click="override_conflict" phx-value-index={conflict.index} > Override
<.button type="button" data-test="save-plan-button" phx-target={@myself} phx-click="save" phx-disable-with="Saving..." > Save Plan
""" end @impl true def update(%{plan: plan} = assigns, socket) do changeset = Scheduling.change_recurring_plan(assigns.current_scope, plan, %{}) {:ok, socket |> assign(assigns) |> assign(:overridden, MapSet.new()) |> assign(:properties, list_properties(assigns.current_scope)) |> assign(:cleaners, Scheduling.list_cleaners(assigns.current_scope)) |> assign_form_and_conflicts(changeset)} end @impl true def handle_event("validate", %{"plan" => params}, socket) do changeset = socket.assigns.current_scope |> Scheduling.change_recurring_plan(socket.assigns.plan, params) |> Map.put(:action, :validate) {:noreply, assign_form_and_conflicts(socket, changeset)} end def handle_event("override_conflict", %{"index" => index}, socket) do index = String.to_integer(index) {:noreply, socket |> Phoenix.Component.update(:overridden, &MapSet.put(&1, index)) |> Phoenix.Component.update( :conflicts, &Enum.reject(&1, fn conflict -> conflict.index == index end) )} end # The save button is a plain `phx-click`, not a form submit — the # board's own conflict-review flow drives it that way (see the # spex). It carries no params of its own, so it saves whatever the # last "validate" pass put in the form. def handle_event("save", %{"plan" => params}, socket), do: save_plan(socket, params) def handle_event("save", _params, socket), do: save_plan(socket, socket.assigns.form.params || %{}) defp save_plan(socket, params) do case Scheduling.create_recurring_plan(socket.assigns.current_scope, params) do {:ok, {plan, _jobs}} -> notify_parent({:saved, plan}) changeset = Scheduling.change_recurring_plan(socket.assigns.current_scope, plan, %{}) {:noreply, socket |> assign(:plan, plan) |> assign_form_and_conflicts(changeset)} {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset, as: :plan))} end end defp assign_form_and_conflicts(socket, changeset) do draft = Ecto.Changeset.apply_changes(changeset) conflicts = socket.assigns.current_scope |> Scheduling.preview_conflicts(draft) |> Enum.reject(&MapSet.member?(socket.assigns.overridden, &1.index)) socket |> assign(:form, to_form(changeset, as: :plan)) |> assign(:conflicts, conflicts) end defp notify_parent(msg), do: send(self(), {__MODULE__, msg}) defp list_properties(%{active_account_id: account_id}) do Property |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id) |> order_by([p], asc: p.service_address) |> Repo.all() end defp property_options(properties), do: Enum.map(properties, &{&1.service_address, &1.id}) defp cleaner_options(cleaners), do: Enum.map(cleaners, &{&1.name || &1.email, &1.id}) defp conflict_reason_text(:unavailable), do: "the cleaner is unavailable that day" defp conflict_reason_text(:overlap), do: "it overlaps another booking" defp form_title(:new), do: "New Recurring Plan" defp form_title(:edit), do: "Edit Recurring Plan" end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.PlanLive do
  @moduledoc """
  Routes for creating (`:new`) or editing (`:edit`) a recurring plan.
  Hosts `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.PlanFormComponent`.
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan
  alias CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.PlanFormComponent

  @impl true
  def render(assigns) do
    ~H"""
    <Layouts.app flash={@flash} current_scope={@current_scope}>
      <.live_component
        module={PlanFormComponent}
        id="plan-form"
        current_scope={@current_scope}
        action={@live_action}
        plan={@plan}
      />
    </Layouts.app>
    """
  end

  @impl true
  def mount(params, _session, socket) do
    {:ok, apply_action(socket, socket.assigns.live_action, params)}
  end

  defp apply_action(socket, :new, _params) do
    assign(socket, :plan, %RecurringPlan{})
  end

  defp apply_action(socket, :edit, %{"id" => id}) do
    assign(socket, :plan, Scheduling.get_recurring_plan!(socket.assigns.current_scope, id))
  end

  # Saving intentionally does not navigate away — the form keeps
  # showing the created series' conflict flags for the owner to
  # review/override afterward (see `PlanFormComponent`).
  @impl true
  def handle_info({PlanFormComponent, {:saved, _plan}}, socket) do
    {:noreply, socket}
  end
end

# Story 846: a job materialized from a recurring plan carries that
  # plan's preferred cleaner as its default assignment (see
  # `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence.job_attrs/1`). Reassigning it to
  # someone else always succeeds — this only flags the deviation for
  # the owner, it's a warning, never a block. A one-off job (no
  # `recurring_plan_id`) or a plan with no preference set (`cleaner_id`
  # nil) never warns, since there's nothing to deviate from.
  defp deviates_from_preferred_cleaner?(_scope, %Job{recurring_plan_id: nil}), do: false

  defp deviates_from_preferred_cleaner?(scope, %Job{} = job) do
    plan = Scheduling.get_recurring_plan!(scope, job.recurring_plan_id)
    not is_nil(plan.cleaner_id) and plan.cleaner_id != job.cleaner_id

# Story 846: a job materialized from a recurring plan carries that
  # plan's preferred cleaner as its default assignment (see
  # `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence.job_attrs/1`). Reassigning it to
  # someone else always succeeds — this only flags the deviation for
  # the owner, it's a warning, never a block. A one-off job (no
  # `recurring_plan_id`) or a plan with no preference set (`cleaner_id`
  # nil) never warns, since there's nothing to deviate from.
  defp deviates_from_preferred_cleaner?(_scope, %Job{recurring_plan_id: nil}), do: false

  defp deviates_from_preferred_cleaner?(scope, %Job{} = job) do
    plan = Scheduling.get_recurring_plan!(scope, job.recurring_plan_id)
    not is_nil(plan.cleaner_id) and plan.cleaner_id != job.cleaner_id
  end

846: RecurringPlan.cleaner_id (preferred cleaner), PlanFormComponent's "Preferred Cleaner" field, and Recurrence.job_attrs/1 defaulting every generated job's cleaner_id to the plan's preference were ALL ALREADY IMPLEMENTED before I touched anything — I confirmed via a throwaway debug test that a plan's materialized job is correctly pre-assigned to the preferred cleaner. I added the one genuinely missing piece: a [data-test='preferred-cleaner-warning'] banner on ScheduleLive.Index, shown when reassign_job's new cleaner differs from the job's originating plan's preferred cleaner (nil for one-off jobs or unset preference — never warns then). Verified working via a throwaway test (warn on deviation, silent otherwise), then deleted that test.

Blocker — all 5 spec files in test/spex/846_.../ share a job_ids/1 helper using regex ~r/data-test="job-(\d+)"/, which only matches numeric IDs. Job has always used UUID (binary_id) primary keys throughout this app (since 833/834), so this regex can never extract a job id from the board — every one of the 5 tests fails at that same `[job_id] = job_ids(html)` line before reaching its actual assertions, regardless of implementation. This looks like a bug in the spec files themselves (assumed integer job ids), not something fixable from schedule_live/scheduling without changing Job's PK type, which would be a large, invasive, out-of-scope change. Recommend routing a regex fix (e.g. match `[0-9a-f-]+`) to whoever owns spec authoring; happy to re-verify immediately once that lands — I'm confident the underlying behavior is already correct for 7196/7199/7205/7206 and now also 7202.

Counts: 846 0/5 (blocked by spec regex, not implementation), 833 7/7, 834 5/5, 840 5/5, 843 7/7, mix test 146/146. No regressions.

Sent to the team lead. Summary of this round:

Story 846's core feature (preferred cleaner on recurring plans, defaulting materialized jobs to that cleaner) turned out to already be fully implemented — I verified it with a throwaway debug test that confirmed a plan's generated job correctly lands in the preferred cleaner's board column. I added the one missing piece: a `[data-test='preferred-cleaner-warning']` banner on `ScheduleLive.Index` that appears when a reassignment deviates from a job's originating plan's preferred cleaner, and stays silent for one-off jobs or plans with no preference set.

All 5 of story 846's spec files fail at the same line, though, before ever reaching their real assertions — they share a `job_ids/1` helper that extracts job IDs with the regex `~r/data-test="job-(\d+)"/`, which only matches digits. This app's `Job` schema has always used UUID primary keys, so that regex can never find a job element on the board. This is a bug in the spec files' own test helper, not something fixable from the scheduling/schedule_live code without changing Job's primary key type across the whole app — I flagged it back to the team lead as a spec-authoring issue rather than attempting a workaround.

Good news on the side: story 843 is now fully green (7/7, up from 5/7), thanks to other agents' concurrent work landing (`push_enabled` on Users, and whatever resolved the escalation path). Full regression check: 832 (9/9), 833 (7/7), 834 (5/5), 837 (6/6), 840 (5/5), 843 (7/7), 846 (0/5, blocked as described), and `mix test` (146/146) — no regressions anywhere.

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.CleanerLive do
  @moduledoc """
  Adds a cleaner to the account's roster by name, so jobs and time off
  can be assigned to them.

  Not one of the schedule live-context's tracked components (only
  `Board`, `PlanFormComponent`, and `JobFormComponent` are) — added as
  minimal supporting scaffolding because every story 833 scenario
  needs a cleaner to exist first. See
  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3` for the fuller,
  login-capable path other stories seed cleaners through.
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  @impl true
  def render(assigns) do
    ~H"""
    <Layouts.app flash={@flash} current_scope={@current_scope}>
      <.header>New Cleaner</.header>

      <.form
        for={@form}
        id="cleaner-form"
        data-test="cleaner-form"
        phx-change="validate"
        phx-submit="save"
      >
        <.input field={@form[:name]} type="text" label="Name" />

        <footer>
          <.button phx-disable-with="Saving...">Save Cleaner</.button>
        </footer>
      </.form>
    </Layouts.app>
    """
  end

  @impl true
  def mount(params, _session, socket) do
    {:ok, apply_action(socket, socket.assigns.live_action, params)}
  end

  defp apply_action(socket, :new, _params) do
    assign(socket, :form, to_form(cleaner_changeset(%{}), as: :cleaner))
  end

  defp apply_action(socket, :show, _params) do
    push_navigate(socket, to: ~p"/schedule")
  end

  @impl true
  def handle_event("validate", %{"cleaner" => params}, socket) do
    {:noreply,
     assign(socket, :form, to_form(cleaner_changeset(params), as: :cleaner, action: :validate))}
  end

  def handle_event("save", %{"cleaner" => %{"name" => name}}, socket) do
    case Scheduling.register_cleaner(socket.assigns.current_scope, name) do
      {:ok, user} ->
        {:noreply, push_navigate(socket, to: ~p"/schedule/cleaners/#{user.id}")}

      {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} ->
        {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset, as: :cleaner))}
    end
  end

  defp cleaner_changeset(params) do
    %User{}
    |> Ecto.Changeset.cast(params, [:name])
    |> Ecto.Changeset.validate_required([:name])
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.AvailabilityLive do
  @moduledoc """
  Records a cleaner's time off (an all-day block, or a partial-day
  window) so the schedule board and conflict detector both know when
  that cleaner is unavailable.

  Not one of the schedule live-context's tracked components — added as
  minimal supporting scaffolding, same as `CleanerLive`.
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.AvailabilityBlock

  @impl true
  def render(assigns) do
    ~H"""
    <Layouts.app flash={@flash} current_scope={@current_scope}>
      <.header>New Time Off</.header>

      <.form
        for={@form}
        id="time-off-form"
        data-test="time-off-form"
        phx-change="validate"
        phx-submit="save"
      >
        <.input field={@form[:date]} type="date" label="Date" />
        <.input field={@form[:all_day]} type="checkbox" label="All day" />
        <.input field={@form[:start_time]} type="time" label="Start Time" />
        <.input field={@form[:end_time]} type="time" label="End Time" />

        <footer>
          <.button phx-disable-with="Saving...">Save Time Off</.button>
        </footer>
      </.form>
    </Layouts.app>
    """
  end

  @impl true
  def mount(%{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}, _session, socket) do
    changeset =
      Scheduling.change_availability_block(
        socket.assigns.current_scope,
        %AvailabilityBlock{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}
      )

    {:ok,
     socket
     |> assign(:cleaner_id, cleaner_id)
     |> assign(:form, to_form(changeset, as: :time_off))}
  end

  @impl true
  def handle_event("validate", %{"time_off" => params}, socket) do
    changeset =
      %AvailabilityBlock{cleaner_id: socket.assigns.cleaner_id}
      |> AvailabilityBlock.changeset(with_cleaner_id(socket, params))
      |> Map.put(:action, :validate)

    {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset, as: :time_off))}
  end

  def handle_event("save", %{"time_off" => params}, socket) do
    case Scheduling.create_availability_block(
           socket.assigns.current_scope,
           with_cleaner_id(socket, params)
         ) do
      {:ok, block} ->
        {:noreply, push_navigate(socket, to: ~p"/schedule/cleaners/#{block.cleaner_id}")}

      {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} ->
        {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset, as: :time_off))}
    end
  end

  defp with_cleaner_id(socket, params),
    do: Map.put(params, "cleaner_id", socket.assigns.cleaner_id)
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.AvailabilityBlock do
  @moduledoc """
  A period when a cleaner is unavailable for assignment — a day off, or
  a partial-day block on a single date.

  `all_day: true` blocks the whole `date` regardless of `start_time`/
  `end_time` (which are ignored/nil in that case). Otherwise the block
  only covers `start_time..end_time` on `date`.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          date: Date.t() | nil,
          all_day: boolean(),
          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "availability_blocks" do
    field :date, :date
    field :all_day, :boolean, default: false
    field :start_time, :time
    field :end_time, :time

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  def changeset(block, attrs) do
    block
    |> cast(attrs, [:cleaner_id, :date, :all_day, :start_time, :end_time])
    |> validate_required([:cleaner_id, :date])
    |> validate_partial_day_times()
  end

  defp validate_partial_day_times(changeset) do
    if get_field(changeset, :all_day) do
      changeset
    else
      validate_required(changeset, [:start_time, :end_time],
        message: "is required for a partial-day block"
      )
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Accounts.MembersRepository do
  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.{Account, Member}
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  def add_user_to_account(user_id, account_id, role \\ :member) do
    %Member{}
    |> Member.changeset(%{user_id: user_id, account_id: account_id, role: role})
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  def remove_user_from_account(user_id, account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Member, user_id: user_id, account_id: account_id) do
      nil ->
        {:error, :not_found}

      member ->
        case member.role do
          :owner ->
            owner_count = count_owners(account_id)
            if owner_count > 1, do: Repo.delete(member), else: {:error, :last_owner}

          _ ->
            Repo.delete(member)
        end
    end
  end

  def update_user_role(user_id, account_id, role) do
    case Repo.get_by(Member, user_id: user_id, account_id: account_id) do
      nil ->
        {:error, :not_found}

      member ->
        changeset = Member.update_role_changeset(member, %{role: role})
        validated_changeset = Member.validate_owner_exists(changeset, Repo)

        case validated_changeset.valid? do
          true -> Repo.update(validated_changeset)
          false -> {:error, validated_changeset}
        end
    end
  end

  def get_user_role(user_id, account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Member, user_id: user_id, account_id: account_id) do
      nil -> nil
      member -> member.role
    end
  end

  def user_has_account_access?(user_id, account_id) do
    Repo.exists?(from m in Member, where: m.user_id == ^user_id and m.account_id == ^account_id)
  end

  def can_add_user_to_account?(_account_id), do: true

  def count_account_users(account_id) do
    Repo.aggregate(from(m in Member, where: m.account_id == ^account_id), :count)
  end

  def list_user_accounts(user_id) do
    from(a in Account,
      join: m in Member,
      on: m.account_id == a.id,
      where: m.user_id == ^user_id
    )
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def list_account_users(account_id) do
    from(u in User,
      join: m in Member,
      on: m.user_id == u.id,
      where: m.account_id == ^account_id
    )
    |> Repo.all()
  end

## Cleaners (account members who take jobs)

  @doc """
  Lists the account's members as candidate cleaners for the board and
  assignment pickers.
  """
  def list_cleaners(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> Accounts.list_account_members(account_id)
    |> Enum.map(& &1.user)
  end

  @doc """
  Registers a new cleaner: a user identified by display name (rather
  than login credentials) added to the account as a member, so jobs
  and availability can be assigned to them. There is no login flow for
  a cleaner created this way — see `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3`
  for the (real, login-capable) path other stories seed cleaners
  through.
  """
  def register_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, name)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(name) do
    with {:ok, user} <- insert_cleaner_user(name),
         {:ok, _member} <- Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account_id, :member) do
      {:ok, user}
    end
  end

  defp insert_cleaner_user(name) do
    %User{}
    |> Ecto.Changeset.cast(%{name: name, email: placeholder_email(name)}, [:name, :email])
    |> Ecto.Changeset.validate_required([:name, :email])
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp placeholder_email(name) do
    slug =
      name
      |> String.downcase()
      |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]+/, ".")
      |> String.trim(".")

    "#{slug}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@cleaners.local"
  end
end
