defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.CleanerLive do
  @moduledoc """
  Adds a cleaner to the account's roster by name, so jobs and time off
  can be assigned to them.

  Not one of the schedule live-context's tracked components (only
  `Board`, `PlanFormComponent`, and `JobFormComponent` are) — added as
  minimal supporting scaffolding because every story 833 scenario
  needs a cleaner to exist first. See
  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3` for the fuller,
  login-capable path other stories seed cleaners through.
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  @impl true
  def render(assigns) do
    ~H"""
    <Layouts.app flash={@flash} current_scope={@current_scope}>
      <.header>New Cleaner</.header>

      <.form
        for={@form}
        id="cleaner-form"
        data-test="cleaner-form"
        phx-change="validate"
        phx-submit="save"
      >
        <.input field={@form[:name]} type="text" label="Name" />

        <footer>
          <.button phx-disable-with="Saving...">Save Cleaner</.button>
        </footer>
      </.form>
    </Layouts.app>
    """
  end

  @impl true
  def mount(params, _session, socket) do
    {:ok, apply_action(socket, socket.assigns.live_action, params)}
  end

  defp apply_action(socket, :new, _params) do
    assign(socket, :form, to_form(cleaner_changeset(%{}), as: :cleaner))
  end

  defp apply_action(socket, :show, _params) do
    push_navigate(socket, to: ~p"/schedule")
  end

  @impl true
  def handle_event("validate", %{"cleaner" => params}, socket) do
    {:noreply,
     assign(socket, :form, to_form(cleaner_changeset(params), as: :cleaner, action: :validate))}
  end

  def handle_event("save", %{"cleaner" => %{"name" => name}}, socket) do
    case Scheduling.register_cleaner(socket.assigns.current_scope, name) do
      {:ok, user} ->
        {:noreply, push_navigate(socket, to: ~p"/schedule/cleaners/#{user.id}")}

      {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} ->
        {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset, as: :cleaner))}
    end
  end

  defp cleaner_changeset(params) do
    %User{}
    |> Ecto.Changeset.cast(params, [:name])
    |> Ecto.Changeset.validate_required([:name])
  end
end

---
name: liveview-phx-change-needs-form
description: phx-change inputs must be inside a <form> — render_change tests pass even when real browsers throw; browser QA is the only catch
metadata:

Found during Cleaner CRM QA (2026-07-07): LiveView inputs/selects with `phx-change` but no `<form>` ancestor throw "form events require the input to be inside a form" in the client JS (pushInput) and silently no-op for real users — while `Phoenix.LiveViewTest.render_change/2` specs stay green because they bypass the client JS entirely (false-positive green bar).

**Why:** This made 3 of 5 acceptance criteria on the weekly dispatch board non-functional in production despite 100% passing BDD specs.

**How to apply:** Every `phx-change`/`phx-submit` control must be wrapped in its own `<form phx-change="...">`. When reviewing LiveView code, grep for `phx-change` outside `<form>`/`<.form>`. Treat render_change-only coverage of interactive controls as unverified until a real browser drives it (see [[no-data-confirm]] for the sibling browser-testability rule).
---confirm-dialog---
---
name: no-data-confirm
description: Never use data-confirm in Phoenix apps — native confirm() is untestable; use the confirm_dialog component pattern
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: b82dc084-1093-4624-b490-31c68a31a4a8
---

John's rule (2026-07-07, during Cleaner CRM QA): do NOT use Phoenix's `data-confirm` attribute. The native `window.confirm()` dialog renders outside the DOM, so Vibium/Playwright/Wallaby cannot observe or click it — every destructive action gated by it is silently untestable in browser automation.

**Why:** QA agents hung indefinitely on pages with data-confirm buttons; this pattern was already replaced in the code_my_spec repo for the same reason.

**How to apply:** Use the `confirm_dialog` CoreComponents pattern instead (ported from `code_my_spec/lib/code_my_spec_web/components/core_components.ex` into `cleaner_crm/lib/cleaner_crm_web/components/core_components.ex`): a DaisyUI `<dialog>` with `show_confirm(id)` as the trigger's phx-click and `on_confirm={JS.push(...)}`; stable selectors `[data-role='confirm-cancel']` / `[data-role='confirm-confirm']`. Note for LiveViewTest specs: the trigger is client-side-only JS (add_class), so specs assert the trigger exists and render_click the dialog's confirm button directly.

I fixed the critical browser-only bug in `lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/schedule_live/index.ex` by wrapping the cleaner-reassign `<select>` and start-time `<input>` each in their own `<form>` element with a stable `id`. On a successful `:assign`, sends `{__MODULE__, {:saved, job}}` to the parent instead (there's nowhere further to go — the parent just refreshes). Two more actions embed this same component inline on `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.Index` (the board) rather than standalone: `:quick_new` (the board's own "New Job" button — same form as `:new`, but sends `{__MODULE__, {:job_created, job}}` to the parent instead of navigating away, since the point is to see the new job's brief on the board itself) and `:edit` (the board's per-job "Edit" button — reschedule and/or price change via `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.update_job/3`, sending `{__MODULE__, {:job_updated, job}}`). <.button phx-disable-with="Saving...">Save Changes
""" end def render(assigns) do ~H"""

@doc """
  Creates a job. Recorded in the audit trail as authored by the
  caller, unless `actor: :system` is passed — used when the job is one
  occurrence materialized from a recurring plan rather than a job a
  human directly asked for (see `create_recurring_plan/2`).
  """
  def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs, opts \\ [])
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, job} <-
           %Job{account_id: account_id}
           |> Job.changeset(attrs)
           |> Repo.insert() do
      record_job_created(scope, job, Keyword.get(opts, :actor, :user))
      {:ok, job}
    end
  end

  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :system) do
    Recorder.record_system(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
  end

  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :user) do
    Recorder.record(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
  end

  # Deliberately omits `scheduled_date`: a "created" entry's own
  # subject label (job → property/client) is enough to identify which
  # job this is, and surfacing it here would read as a schedule change
  # (`field_changes/1`'s "Scheduled date: ..." line) indistinguishable
  # from an actual reschedule recorded later by `update_job/3`.
  defp job_created_values(job) do
    %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id}
  end

  cleaner/property/client preloaded, ordered for the board.
  """

      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    week_end = Date.add(week_start, 6)

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date >= ^week_start and
        j.scheduled_date <= ^week_end and j.status != :cancelled

Root cause: jobs created via the board's "New Job" form (and jobs materialized from a recurring plan) only ever carried a property_id, never a client_id, so job.client_id was always nil unless a caller set it directly (only test fixtures did). Billing code that reads job.client_id directly (invoice rendering, card-on-file charge lookup) therefore had nothing to find.

Fix (lib/cleaner_crm/scheduling.ex only): added derive_client_id/2, called from both create_job/3 and update_job/3. When client_id is blank but property_id is present, it looks up the property (scoped to the account) and backfills client_id from property.client_id before the changeset cast -- careful to match the attrs map's existing key style (atom vs string), since Ecto.Changeset.cast/4 raises on mixed-key maps. A caller that already supplies client_id directly (e.g. fixtures with only a client on hand) is left untouched.

Verified: a throwaway test confirmed both the board's job-creation form and recurring-plan materialization now produce jobs with the correct client_id matching their property's client. mix spex on 832 (9/9), 833 (7/7), 834 (5/5), 836 (6/6); mix test 146/146, no regressions. mix format clean. No dev-env mix compile was run.
